LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin predict this weekend's top games Getty Images What did we learn in Week 6? The Houston Texans are officially back, as is Caleb Williams with the Chicago Bears , and we have some serious questions about the Los Angeles Rams , who were upset by the Arizona Cardinals at home last Sunday. The Cardinals now have more wins at SoFi Stadium this year than the Rams and Los Angeles Chargers combined. This week, the Pittsburgh Steelers and New Orleans Saints will play the first-ever NFL game in Paris, the San Francisco 49ers look to remain perfect against the Atlanta Falcons , and Kenneth Walker III aims to lead the Kansas City Chiefs to victory over his former team, the Seattle Seahawks . This could be a revenge game for the ages. Which teams should you pick in Week 7, and which should you fade? CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin are here to break down the biggest games of the weekend. For clarity, lines for these selections were taken on Oct. 21 over at DraftKings Sportsbook. New England Patriots at Chicago Bears (-3) (TNF) Dajani (Bears -3): I can't remember the last time I've been this excited for a Thursday night game. Caleb Williams will suit up for the first time at home since his hamstring injury, and this is the first Bears home game since the passing of Mike Ditka. I have concerns about this Bears pass defense and how it will fare against a red-hot Drake Maye , but the fact is that Chicago has allowed 9.3 points per game at home this season. The Bears' offense has also averaged 35 points per game in their four wins, and I think Williams is out to make a statement. This will be a high-flying affair that comes down to the very end, and a push is very much in play. But give me Chicago at home, with the backing of an emotionally charged atmosphere. Remember, the Bears' lone Super Bowl win came against the New England Patriots under Ditka. … Prediction: Bears 28, Patriots 24 Dubin (Bears -3): I also see this being a high-scoring game, with two offenses that can pile up points quickly. Chicago's offense in two non-rain/non-Brian Flores games with Caleb Williams under center has been electric, particularly on the ground, and Caleb Williams opens things up for the passing game. New England is struggling to run the ball, but Drake Maye has been on fire as of late. I'll lean toward the Bears here because of the Patriots' injury issues along the offensive line, which could hold the run game back further and put even more on Maye's shoulders. … Prediction: Bears 31, Patriots 27 Pittsburgh Steelers (-3.5) vs. New Orleans Saints (Paris) Dajani (Saints +3.5): The Steelers are impossible to figure out. From week-to-week — or even half-to-half, as evidenced by last week's overtime victory against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers . If you're going to give me the hook at +3.5 in an international game, I'm probably going to take it. The Saints are a perfect 8-0 ATS in their last eight games away from home, and are 3-0 ATS all-time in international games. I think Gayle Benson's recent comments stirred up the locker room, and the Saints responded with a win in which they dropped 34 points — even if it came against the New York Giants . … Prediction: Steelers 23, Saints 20 Dubin (Steelers -3.5): The Saints finally played a game from ahead last week against the Giants, and they didn't necessarily look comfortable doing it. They have mostly been a second-half offensive team throughout this season, struggling early on before piling up yards and points in comeback mode. I don't trust this offense enough to build a lead against Pittsburgh's defense (ninth in yards, 12th in points, fifth in EPA per play) right now, so I'll lean toward this game playing out in a similar fashion to New Orleans' early-season contests, with the Steelers taking a lead and the Saints trying to stage a comeback, only to fail this time around. … Prediction: Steelers 21, Saints 17 San Francisco 49ers (-3) at Atlanta Falcons Dajani (Falcons +3): I'm thinking about backing the Falcons in this spot. The 49ers had an emotional victory over the Seahawks in Week 5 and are now on a short week after Monday night's win against the Washington Commanders . It looked like we were in for a blowout after the 49ers went up 23-3, but Washington then outscored San Francisco, 14-0, while outgaining the 49ers 201 yards to 7 yards. That was ... interesting to see. The 49ers have found a way to keep winning games despite all of the injuries. Nick Bosa , Mike Evans , Deebo Samuel , Upton Stout and Mykel Williams were among the players who did not practice on Wednesday. This week, I'm going to take the points with Atlanta. … Prediction: 49ers 22, Falcons 20 Dubin (49ers -3): This line feels several points too low, even with Mike Evans potentially out in addition to all of the other wide receiver issues. So long as the Niners have Kyle Shanahan calling plays and Brock Purdy , Christian McCaffrey and George Kittle involved, I think their offense cooks. And Atlanta can't quite reach the same level offensively — even with Bijan Robinson and Drake London on hand. The Niners have been excellent against the run this year, and if this game winds up being one where Penix has to match Purdy throw for throw, I don't see that going well for Atlanta. … Prediction: 49ers 26, Falcons 16 Cincinnati Bengals at Baltimore Ravens (-3) Dajani ( Bengals +3): The Bengals are fresh off their bye while the Baltimore Ravens are fresh off ... a loss to the Cleveland Browns . It was their 15th loss when leading by at least seven points in the fourth quarter since 2020, which ranks the most in the NFL. Lamar Jackson has a chance to return this week, but I'm curious to see how "spry" he looks. The two-time NFL MVP was playing some fantastic ball before the unfortunate ankle injury, and it's worth mentioning he's 7-2 in his career against Joe Burrow . I was high on the Bengals entering this season, and I'm not ready to move off that take. I think this Baltimore secondary is in for a tough test in stopping Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins . The former averages 120.4 receiving yards per game vs. the Ravens, while the latter caught two touchdowns the last time he faced them. Higgins actually hasn't faced Baltimore since Oct. 6, 2024! It's been a while. Give me the upset here. We aren't 100% sure if Jackson is even returning to the lineup, and he'll have to face one of the best interior pass rushes in the NFL. Dexter Lawrence , Jonathan Allen and Kris Jenkins Jr. are the only defensive tackle trio to record multiple sacks this season. … Prediction: Bengals 29, Ravens 27 Dubin (Ravens -3): I'm assuming that Lamar Jackson is back for this game. If he's not, then you can switch my pick to the Bengals. If Jackson is in alongside Derrick Henry and Zay Flowers , I just don't think this Baltimore offense can be stopped. When those three have shared the field this season, the Ravens are averaging 9.9 yards per play. NINE POINT NINE. Unfortunately, the sample size is only 63 plays due to injuries to Jackson and Flowers at different times. If there is any team that can compete with an explosive offense, it's probably the Bengals, but I don't see them quite keeping up here. … Prediction: Ravens 30, Bengals 26 Green Bay Packers at Detroit Lions (-3) Dajani ( Lions -3): Just take the Over in this matchup. The Lions really burned me coming off the bye last year, losing to J.J. McCarthy , but I'm going to back them in this spot. The concern is, of course, the defense, which ranks dead last in the NFL with 404.4 total yards surrendered per game. HOWEVER, I will mention that Kelvin Sheppard 's unit forced five straight three-and-outs from the Cardinals in that 45-21 win in Week 5. Plus, Brian Branch is set to return to the lineup as well. Give me the Lions at home. … Prediction: Lions 35, Packers 30 Dubin (Lions -3): This one has all the makings of a shootout, with two explosive offenses going back and forth. Jared Goff and Co. are coming off the bye, and they have scored 31 or more points in four of their five games to date — and they scored 26 while piling up 452 yards in the other one. Nobody except maybe Kenneth Walker III is doing it at a higher level than Jahmyr Gibbs right now, either. Meanwhile, Green Bay can throw the ball all over the yard, and everyone throws it on the Lions. Maybe Green Bay can actually run with some efficiency in Josh Jacobs ' potential return, but it's not like he was all that efficient last season, either. I lean toward the Lions because they can beat you both ways. … Prediction: Lions 34, Packers 28 Kansas City Chiefs at Seattle Seahawks (-2.5) (SNF) Dajani (Chiefs +2.5): The Seahawks looked completely disinterested in that Week 6 loss to the Denver Broncos . McCarthy , but we will see. No matter who starts, the Texans ' defense is having issues. The Giants will move the ball. But they won't stop C.J. Stroud . He's on fire and that gets the Texans the victory. The New England Patriots and Drake Maye are riding a three-game winning streak into their primetime matchup with the Chicago Bears and former No. 1 overall pick Caleb Williams on Thursday Night Football. Williams is making his second straight start after he missed three games earlier this season with a hamstring injury. The star quarterback showed no signs of rust in Week 6, completing 30 of his 36 pass attempts in a win over the Atlanta Falcons, improving the Bears to 4-2 this season. Chicago is favored in this matchup, and it needs every win it can get with the NFC North sporting four teams over .500 through the first six weeks. The Bears may be getting a little extra love in this matchup because of all the injuries for the Patriots, who have been decimated at receiver (Mack Hollins and Romeo Doubs on IR) and on their offensive line. Still, New England has won three games in a row, and Maye is back in the MVP conversation with 10 touchdown passes during that streak. He has a tough matchup ahead against a Chicago team that is in the top 10 in the league in EPA/Play and success rate on defense this season. So, how should bettors attack Thursday’s showdown? In the leadup to this marquee matchup, the SI Betting team has made a bunch of game picks, prop bet selections and more. I’ve decided to share some of our favorites all in one place to help bettors get the most of this primetime matchup between two playoff contenders in Week 7. Best NFL Picks and Predictions for Patriots vs. Bears Odds via DraftKings Sportsbook New England Patriots vs. Chicago Bears UNDER 50.5 (-105) – Iain MacMillan Drake Maye OVER 1.5 Passing Touchdowns (-116) – Peter Dewey Colston Loveland Anytime TD (+170) – Peter Dewey D’Andre Swift UNDER 61.5 Rushing Yards (-115) – Peter Dewey This week, SI Betting’s Iain MacMillan shared his favorite bet for this matchup in his Road to 272 column , where he picks every game of the NFL season. He’s taking the UNDER even with two star quarterbacks facing off: Unless I'm missing something, I'm not quite sure why the total for this game is in the 50s. Sure, the Bears' offense is much more explosive with Caleb Williams at quarterback, but even with that being the case, these two offenses rank 12th and 14th in EPA per play this season and seventh and 12th in success rate. A high total would make sense if the two defenses in this game were bad, but they rank in the top half of the league in most metrics. In fact, the Bears' defense comes into this game ranking fourth in opponent success rate. The Patriots' offense is also dealing with some injuries. A.J. Brown is questionable, and Romeo Doubs is on IR. Their run game can't be relied on to help out the injuries at wide receiver, as it's been largely ineffective all season. I'll bet the UNDER on Thursday Night Football for the second straight week. Maye started the season in an awful slump, throwing just one score and six picks in his first three games. Since then, he’s flipped the script, tossing 10 scores (at least three in each game) over the last three weeks, leading New England to wins over Buffalo, Las Vegas and the New York Jets. Maye is right back in the mix to win the MVP, and I like this matchup against a Chicago defense that has allowed nine passing scores in 2026 and was torched by Bryce Young and Jordan Love already this season. The Bears have benefitted from some soft scheduling in terms of the quarterbacks they’ve faced, but Love threw for 367 yards against them in Week 5, and Chicago has allowed the 15th-most passing yards in the league. New England loves to throw the ball, and I think the odds for this prop are pretty favorable considering the fact that Maye threw 31 touchdown passes in 2025. Bears tight end Colston Loveland had a breakout showing in Week 6, catching six of his seven targets for 65 yards and a score. Williams only threw one touchdown in Week 6, but Loveland was targeted multiple times in the end zone – Caleb just missed him for a second score. Last season, the young tight end really came on in the second half, finishing the campaign with six touchdown receptions. He’s only picked up one in 2026, and New England has allowed just one receiving score to the position this season. Still, Loveland’s role is growing with 21 targets over the last three games. He’s a solid bet at this price after his best game of the season. D’Andre Swift has a ton of carries for the Bears this season, handling 94 touches for 398 yards and six scores on the ground, but he hasn’t been super efficient since Week 1. Swift ran for 124 yards on 18 carries against Carolina in the season opener, yet he has just one other game (Week 3 against Philadelphia) where he’s picked up over 60 rushing yards. Backup Kyle Monangai (turf toe) has been banged up, but Swift still split time with Roschon Johnson in Week 6 and has played just 56.7 percent of the Bears’ snaps this season. New England is allowing just 3.9 yards per carry in the 2026 campaign, and I wouldn’t be shocked if Swift came up short of this rushing total again on Thursday. He has averaged less than four yards per carry in two of the last three weeks, putting up 58, 43 and 44 rushing yards during that stretch. Even if the volume is there for the veteran back, I think he’s a fade candidate in Week 7. Odds refresh periodically and are subject to change. away.blurb: The New England Patriots will likely roll out a shorthanded squad on Thursday for their primetime matchup against the Bears at Soldier Field. Speaking after Sunday's win, Coach Mike Vrabel was candid about the availability of his banged-up players, especially in an abbreviated week with little downtime available. "It's a short week," Vrabel said. "So whether they can make it back or not, I don't know. They don't finish the game. We'll have to see. But I don't know [anything] other than that. And we'll just have to figure out who we have available and find 48 [players] to put out there. So it's just hard to say, but it's a short week. And if you don't finish the game, that's a quick turnaround." It was just a walkthrough, but Moses' "limited" status at least offers some sliver of hope that the veteran tackle could be back on the gridiron for Thursday's game against the Bears. home.blurb: Jonah Jackson will gut it out and play for the Bears in Week 7 It's big for Jackson to be coming back, but his ability to gut it out through the injury speaks to his toughness. Bears fans hope he can stay healthy. Monangai was one of the two Bears players who has been ruled out for the Patriots game with his thumb/toe injury, but the main concern is the toe. This will be the third game he has missed in a row since the injury. In the other big injury news, linebacker T.J. Edwards was listed as doubtful and will most likely not play a second straight game with the hamstring injury. D'Marco Jackson will be replacing Edwards in the lineup if he truly can't go. Cornerback Tyrique Stevenson is listed as questionable with the hip injury. If Stevenson can't go, it will be Malik Muhammad starting on the outside. The Chicago Bears are preparing for their Week 7 Thursday Night Football showdown with the New England Patriots , with key injury news ahead of the contest. This season has been considerably better for the Bears in terms of injuries than it was last year, but there are still some key players to watch who are dealing with injuries. From Kyle Monangai's toe to Jonah Jackson's hip/quad, the Bears are navigating some of their top injuries. Here's how all six players on the injury report are doing going into the contest. Jackson left early in the Bears' Week 6 win over the Atlanta Falcons with a hip/quad injury. Luke Newman replaced him and finished the game at right guard. At the start of the week, it didn't look like Jackson would play, as ESPN NFL reporter Jeremy Fowler said he would be week-to-week. Then the Bears' final injury report said he was a full participant on Wednesday and had no injury designation. Having Jackson in the lineup is huge for the offensive line, as he is having the best season of his career. In 244 pass-blocking snaps, he has allowed nine pressures and one quarterback hit. Pro Football Focus gave him an 83.7 overall grade, ranking him sixth among 77 eligible guards. Kyle Monangai is close to returning, but will miss third straight game This season, Monangai has rushed for 324 yards and three touchdowns, averaging 5.4 yards per carry. He was in the top-10 in the NFL in rushing yards and touchdowns before his injury. It will be D'Andre Swift and Roschon Johnson carrying the load in the backfield for the time being, but it may not last long. The latest update from NFL insider Ian Rapoport seems to be that Monangai could be coming back in the next week, so something to keep an eye on for Bears fans. Looking over rest of Bears' injured players Another linebacker, Jack Sanborn, will not be playing in the game with a concussion, as he was not able to clear it quick enough. That is more of a hit with the special teams unit for the Bears. home.headline: What we learned about Caleb Williams and Chicago Bears in NFL Week 6
home.source: USA TODAY College Sports Wire on MSN
home.blurb: The Chicago Bears were ignited by the return of former USC Trojan Caleb Williams and teammate Kyler Gordon. Both players did not miss a beat and put together dominant performances. As a result, the Bears ' offense and defense both looked good enough to make a run at the Super Bowl. Coltson Loveland was disappointing at the start of the season. Last week, however, the return of starting quarterback Caleb Williams helped him get his confidence back. Loveland had a spectacular touchdown catch on the opening drive, and he finished with 6 catches for 65 yards. The Bears offense is at its best when Loveland is making plays. It looks like the Bears' biggest playmaker is back. The NFC conference is wide open and up for grabs. The San Francisco 49ers and the Minnesota Vikings are both undefeated, but both teams have weaknesses the Bears can exploit. When this Bears team is healthy and with the return of Kyle Monangai on offense, the Bears can beat anyone in the league. Here is what we learned about the Bears in NFL Week 6: Caleb Williams looks like a top 5 quarterback One of the biggest weaknesses of Caleb Williams' game is his accuracy and his ability to play on time. Against the Atlanta Falcons, those weaknesses looked like strengths. Caleb started the game off 24/24, not missing a beat. He finished the game with an 83.3% completion percentage. That proves Caleb Williams is one of the best quarterbacks in the league. Right now, he leads the NFL with a 72.5% completion percentage. His development in year 3 has been exciting to watch and scary for the rest of the NFL to see. Kyle Monangai is such a pivotal piece to the offense Without Kyle Monangai, the Bears' run game has taken a big hit. He is the physical back that this offense needs. Without him, D'Andre Swift is a lot easier to limit. In his last game, Monangai had 30 carries for 146 yards and a touchdown. Through just 4 games, he has 324 yards and 3 touchdowns. In his absence, his true value to the offense has been on full display. It was too early to close the door on Colston Loveland When healthy Kyler Gordon is one of the best at his position in the NFL In only 16 snaps, Kyler Gordon showed he can make a massive impact. He tallied 3 sacks and a tackle for a loss on his first snap of the season. Dennis Allen is able to get extremely creative when Kyler Gordon is on the field. Gordon could be the key to the Bears' defense going from good to great. On Wednesday, the Patriots ruled out LG Alijah Vera-Tucker (hamstring), RG Ben Brown (knee), CB Carlton Davis III (neck), CB Karon Prunty (hamstring), and CB Channing Canada (hamstring). The Patriots are also listing RT Morgan Moses (foot), S Kevin Byard III (chest), S Craig Woodson (shoulder), and LB Christian Ellliss (chest) as questionable for Thursday night's game. Starting on offense, the Patriots offensive line will be shorthanded, with the Pats down multiple guards who have started games this season. Along with starting RG Mike Onwenu (ankle) and top backup Greg Van Roten (thigh), who are on injured reserve, New England is also down Vera-Tucker (hamstring) and Brown (knee). In his final press conference before Thursday night's game, head coach Mike Vrabel confirmed that Walter Rouse and Matt Pryor will start vs. the Bears. The Pats projected starting offensive line is LT Will Campbell, LG Walter Rouse, C Jared Wilson, RG Matt Pryor, and RT Morgan Moses (questionable) or Caleb Lomu. If Moses can't finish the game and the Patriots start Lomu at guard, the rookie would need to kick back outside. Vrabel also hinted at Lomu being prepared to be the backup center. In short, that's a lot of moving parts to plan for in-game contingencies, so the clearest path forward is to start Rouse and Pryor at guard while Lomu continues in his role as the top swing tackle. Plus, Moses is listed as questionable, and if he doesn't play on the short week, Lomu would make his first NFL start at right tackle. At the skill positions, the Patriots are down two wide receivers, Doubs and Hollins, both on injured reserve. However, the Pats will have top WR A.J. Brown, whose ankle is off the injury report. New England's available wideouts are Brown, DeMario Douglas, Kyle Williams, and Efton Chism III, while OC Josh McDaniels can use all his tight ends and running backs. The Patriots could elevate a fifth wide receiver from the practice squad, but that feels unlikely with limited game-day roster spots. Pittsburgh is 4-2 after a 26-19 overtime win over Tampa Bay, while New Orleans is 2-4 after beating the Giants 34-27. Kickoff is scheduled for 9:30 a.m. ET. With both teams coming off big wins in Week 6, let's take a look at the matchup and the bold predictions for Week 7 in Paris, France. Chris Boswell kicks five field goals, two from 50-plus © Joseph Maiorana-Imagn Images Boswell is 13-for-17 on field goals this season, including 4-for-6 from 50-plus yards. Against Tampa Bay he went 4-for-5, with makes from 52 and 58 yards. That was his second straight game with multiple field goals. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) New Orleans allows 29.7 points and 377.7 yards per game. Those numbers suggest Pittsburgh will move the ball. Some of those drives will stall before the end zone, and that is where Boswell scores. The prediction goes beyond another solid outing. Boswell makes five field goals, including two from beyond 50 yards. The limitation is his four misses this season, which show he is not automatic from long range. Tyler Shough throws two interceptions Shough has a 12:5 touchdown-to-interception ratio through six games. He threw only 144 yards against the Giants, though he scored four touchdowns in total. He is also playing through broken bones in his non-throwing hand, which may explain why he has just 242 passing yards over the last two weeks. Predicting two interceptions means Shough nearly matches his early-season total in one afternoon. The route to that outcome is straightforward. Pittsburgh's lead will push New Orleans into longer passing situations, and an injured hand makes tight-window throws harder. The call is that one pass is tipped and picked off in the second half, while another is forced into coverage on a late drive. Those turnovers would turn a competitive game into a Steelers cushion. There is a counterpoint. Shough has produced touchdowns despite modest yardage, so this prediction depends on game script more than on his recent efficiency. Chris Olave posts 120 yards and two touchdowns in a losing rally Olave had double-digit targets in each of the first four games. Over the last two he has seen only 13 targets, producing an 8-89-1 line. That drop in volume looks like the sort of dip that corrects itself. Pittsburgh's defense will give him room to correct it. New Orleans' opponents have averaged 256.0 passing yards per game, which suggests quarterbacks can find openings in this matchup. Rookie Germie Bernard's 11-catch, 87-yard, one-touchdown game against the Steelers' last opponent shows how that kind of volume can arise. Olave reaches 10 targets, 120 yards and two touchdowns as New Orleans chases points. Those scores help the Saints cut a two-score deficit to three points late in the fourth quarter. Pittsburgh still holds on. The prediction is Steelers 31, Saints 27, with Boswell's late field goal sealing it. If Jordyn Tyson makes his debut after traveling with the team while recovering from a hamstring injury, the Saints' receiving group could be even more dangerous. These are deliberately high-variance predictions, not the most likely outcomes. The underlying numbers favor Pittsburgh, but turnovers and a motivated passing offense can make this matchup less predictable than the records suggest. For the first time in the league's long existence, a regular season game will be played in France. Paris, to be exact. After nearly 20 years since the Dolphins and Giants played the first regular season game outside of North America, the NFL's international footprint grows larger every year. As interesting as all of that is, the football played on the field is what really matters. Pittsburgh enters Week 7 with a 4-2 record, barely beating the Buccaneers 26-19 in overtime a week ago. The Saints, meanwhile, climbed to 2-4 after a bizarre 34-27 win over the Giants. Both teams have plenty of flaws they are hoping to correct as the season goes on, but the Steelers are favored for a reason. As the game approaches, we will have all of the important details you need to know. Injury reports, weather reports, how to watch, storylines, and more. So bookmark this page and come back throughout the week! How to Watch Pittsburgh Steelers vs New Orleans Saints in Week 7 Date: Sunday, October 25 Time: 9:30 a.m. EST TV Network: NFL Network Announcers: Dave Pasch (Play-by-Play), Kurt Warner and Jason Kelce (Color Analysts), Molly McGrath (Sideline Reporter) Pittsburgh Steelers Injury Report for Week 7 Steelers injury reports will appear here as they become available New Orleans Saints Injury Report for Week 7 Saints injury reports will appear here as they become available Weather Forecast for Pittsburgh Steelers vs New Orleans Saints Week 7 Current Forecast ( via NFLWeather.com ) Temperature: TBD Wind Speed: TBD Precipitation: TBD Biggest Pittsburgh Steelers Storylines heading into Week 7 Will the Steelers continue leaning on the passing game despite missing multiple playmakers? Despite missing multiple receivers heading into their Week 6 matchup with the Buccaneers, the Steelers chose to make the passing game the focal point of the offense. While they ultimately came away with the victory, it was an ugly mess for much of the contest. Aaron Rodgers put up a solid 253 yards through the air, but it took him a whopping 49 pass attempts to get there. He was the definition of a checkdown merchant , with just five of those 49 passes traveling beyond 10 yards, according to Next Gen Stats . It seemed as though Mike McCarthy didn't have faith that Jaylen Warren and Rico Dowdle could succeed against the Buccaneers' stout run defense. Still, the Steelers can't win games against good teams with that offensive approach. The Saints could be a team that they can once again get away with it against, but it's something to monitor. Which team will handle the international trip better? There has been plenty of discourse surrounding how to handle playing across the pond ever since the NFL's International Series took shape. We saw the Rams be criticized for arriving in Australia right before their Week 1 disaster against the 49ers, who had been down under for days at that point. In the Steelers case, they are taking the route of trying to make the week feel as normal as possible, choosing to fly out on Thursday evening. Meanwhile, the Saints arrived in France on Monday, so they will be well adjusted by game time on Sunday. Will the contrasting strategies make any difference? Only time will tell. Can the Steelers pass rush come alive against a struggling Saints offensive line? The Steelers' pass rush has long been the strength of their defense, but they haven't been as effective on a down-to-down basis this season. According to Sumer Sports , Pittsburgh ranks just 23rd in pressure percentage at 37.4%. They do rank ninth in sacks with 16, so they have managed to get the QB on the ground at an above-average level. Still, they aren't causing as much disruption as they need to be, considering the names in that group. T.J. Watt has cooled off after a hot start, Alex Highsmith isn't having his best season, and Nick Herbig has made splash plays but hasn't been as dominant as he was last season. The interior has been hot and cold, with Cam Heyward remaining a consistent presence while the other pieces have been hit-or-miss. With the Saints missing star left tackle Kaleb Banks, this is an opportunity for them to really hit their stride. If they don't, it may be time to worry. The entire division is over .500, and three teams are 4-2. Every game is critical, and the Steelers look to continue their winning streak with a win over the New Orleans Saints in Paris, France. Buccaneers vs. Steelers: Final injury report for Week 6
away.blurb: The Tampa Bay Buccaneers have released their final injury report ahead of Sunday's Week 6 matchup against the Pittsburgh Steelers, and several key players will be unavailable as Tampa Bay looks to build on last week's victory over Dallas. Quarterback Baker Mayfield (right thumb) has officially been ruled out after missing all three practices this week. Rookie Jalon Daniels will make his third consecutive start after leading the Buccaneers to their first victory of the season last Thursday against the Cowboys. The Buccaneers will also be without safety Antoine Winfield Jr. (rib), who did not participate in practice throughout the week. Wide receiver David Sills V (hamstring) was also ruled out despite being listed as a full participant in all three practices. Cornerback Benjamin Morrison (quad) is listed as doubtful, while linebackers SirVocea Dennis (ankle/foot) and Josiah Trotter (knee), cornerback Ayden Garnes (ankle), and running back Sean Tucker (quad) are questionable. Dennis and Garnes were full participants Friday, providing some encouraging news heading into the weekend. Pittsburgh is also dealing with several injuries, particularly at wide receiver. Roman Wilson (finger) and Ben Skowronek (calf) have been ruled out, along with safety DeShon Elliott (knee). Wide receiver DK Metcalf was added to Friday's report with an illness and is questionable. For the first time in the league's long existence, a regular season game will be played in France. Paris, to be exact. After nearly 20 years since the Dolphins and Giants played the first regular season game outside of North America, the NFL's international footprint grows larger every year. As interesting as all of that is, the football played on the field is what really matters. Pittsburgh enters Week 7 with a 4-2 record, barely beating the Buccaneers 26-19 in overtime a week ago. The Saints, meanwhile, climbed to 2-4 after a bizarre 34-27 win over the Giants. Both teams have plenty of flaws they are hoping to correct as the season goes on, but the Steelers are favored for a reason. While they ultimately came away with the victory, it was an ugly mess for much of the contest. Aaron Rodgers put up a solid 253 yards through the air, but it took him a whopping 49 pass attempts to get there. He was the definition of a checkdown merchant , with just five of those 49 passes traveling beyond 10 yards, according to Next Gen Stats .

For the first time in a few weeks, they “lost” against the spread on Monday. The Niners are still 5-2 against the spread, with the NFL’s second-highest margin of victory at 11.2. They’re also tied for a league-high average margin of victory. So, when media members ask this: I would say the answer is no. Faithful, take 49ers game day wherever you go! The matchup against the Atlanta Falcons always looked like a scheduled loss, if there ever was one. The 49ers are 3-point road favorites, with the total on the game sitting at 49.5 on FanDuel Sportsbook . A high total and a low spread hint at a coin-flip game. We’ll see if Mike Evans plays. On the outside, it makes more sense to give Evans two weeks off so the Achilles soreness goes away and allows Evans to complete a game. But Kyle Shanahan seems to be putting the ball in Evans’s court. If the veteran feels healthy enough to play, he’ll play, even if the team knows they could lose him mid-game. There’s familiarity here, as Raheem Morris takes on his old team. Falcons defensive coordinator Jeff Ulbrich is one of the best in the league and worked with Shanahan in Atlanta a decade ago, not to mention as Morris’s defensive coordinator. Morris will need to find a way to limit Drake London, who has the 8th-highest target share among all NFL receivers. The Falcons throw it to London over 28% of the time. London is 11th in EPA per target. Not far behind London is his teammate Jahan Dotson, who is 14th in EPA per target. Tight end Kyle Pitts is fifth in EPA per target among tight ends. Atlanta is not short on weapons, and we haven’t even gotten to their biggest threat. Bijan Robinson is second in the NFL, averaging 5.77 yards per carry. He averages more yards after contact (4.64) than a good chunk of running backs do per carry. Robinson is a walking highlight who is heavily involved in Atlanta’s passing attack. Michael Penix is limited when it comes to being mobile, so that should work in the Niners favor. If there’s one person you’d want to attempt to slow down the Falcons, it’s the coach who drafted most of these players and watched them practice for the past few years: Raheem Morris. On the other side of the ball, no team has been better against the run than the Falcons defense. They’re first in EPA per rush and sixth in rushing success rate. Atlanta has allowed the third-fewest 10+ yard runs and is seventh in the percentage of runs they stuff. They make teams one-dimensional. This will be a Brock Purdy game. The Falcons won’t blitz Purdy nearly as often as Washington does, but they get pressure with four. That’s a big difference. Atlanta is fourth in pressure rate despite blitzing 23.7% of the time (26th in the NFL). You can throw on this defense. Atlanta is 20th and 21st in EPA per pass and passing success rate. Caleb Williams carved up the Dirty Birds for over 300 passing yards a week ago. A good chunk of those came in the first half. Luther Burden and Colston Loveland had him a day. Tyler Huntley was efficient in Week 5 at Atlanta. He threw for only 201 yards, but completed 75% of his passes and threw two touchdowns. Huntley was efficient in Week 5 at Atlanta. He only threw for 201 yards, but completed 75% of his passes and threw for two touchdowns. Rashod Bateman and Zay Flowers combined for 13 receptions for 115 yards. The week before, Tyler Shough threw the ball 48 times for 286 yards. Chris Olave had 116 yards. Of course, it’s far-fetched to imagine the Niners having a 100-yard receiver without Evans, but Shanahan has a full week to scheme up the non-Evans wideouts. A short road week with an early start on the East Coast, potentially without your leading receiver, against a team that has lost back-to-back games where they feel like they should have won. And the familiarity, paired with the weapons the Falcons have, makes this an intriguing game and a difficult schedule spot for a 6-0 team that could be feeling fat and happy a week away from the bye. away.blurb: With that being said, it leaves the door open for a possible trade in the coming weeks, and one name to keep an eye on is Indianapolis Colts ‘ WR Josh Downs, who could be made available if the Colts don't pick up wins in the next few weeks. San Francisco 49ers Trade Prediction Lands Colts' WR Amid Mike Evans Speculation Unlock the latest Heavy on 49ers news — direct to your inbox. Updated Oct 22, 2026 at 11:40am San Francisco 49ers star wide receiver Mike Evans had to be removed from the team's Monday Night Victory over the Washington Commanders due to an Achilles issue. After the game, reports surfaced that it's likely Evans will be dealing with his Achilles tendinitis for the majority of the season, so the 49ers might want to take it carefully with their No. 1 wideout, especially with a 6-0 start to the season. 49ers Trade Idea Lands Colts' Josh Downs In this trade pitch between the 49ers and Colts, Indianapolis would send San Francisco wide receiver Josh Downs in exchange for a 4th-round draft pick. The 49ers might be absent Mike Evans for a while moving forward after he left Monday night's game against the Chiefs with Achilles tendon soreness. His injury sheet this season looks like the hospital chart for a guy the ambulance just brought into the ER after a major car wreck, and Evans is just one of several pass-catchers the 49ers have lost, to one degree or another, due to injury this season. Meanwhile, the Colts are probably sellers in the coming weeks, and Downs is still a young WR with upside. At 25 years old and in the final year of his rookie contract, Downs would be easy to absorb into the salary cap and can offer SF some much-needed youth, durability, depth, and talent in the WR room. Should the 49ers Pursue Josh Downs? If the Mike Evans Achilles issue may actually put his status in jeopardy for the next handful of weeks, yes, it would be wise to pursue Josh Downs in the trade market, but San Francisco must be mindful that there could be other suitors across the NFL with the same idea of trading for an impact receiver like Josh Downs. In 2026, Downs has 24 catches for 289 receiving yards and has been fairly productive with less-than-solid QB play. away.headline: Joey Bosa NFL Comeback Talk? Free agent tipped for 49ers return; speculation links brothers
away.source: The Times of India on MSN
away.blurb: Four months later, that opportunity arose. Isn’t now the best time to return? Also, the big games may be starting soon. He could be that major boost for the 49ers - when they truly need it the most. Joey Bosa retirement rumors have been circulating throughout the 2026 offseason. They may have halted for a second into the season. Get breaking news anytime, anywhere. Download the TOI app now! But with six games played and Nick Bosa missing four of them for the San Francisco 49ers, the rumors are back in action. Only this time, there’s a spice of an NFL comeback, with midseason urgency. Bleacher Report’s Alex Kay has identified Joey Bosa as a potential addition for San Francisco. The 49ers are navigating defensive-line injury concerns; the veteran edge rusher could become an ideal solution for a team looking to strengthen its pass rush during the 2026 NFL season. Joey Bosa’s reunion with Nick Bosa in San Francisco 49ers Nick Bosa’s Week 2 calf injury has severely affected the franchise’s ability to attack quarterbacks from the edge. Signing Nick Bosa’s older brother, Joey Bosa, could help address that weakness. Not just that, but also pursue a forever dream of championship success. The 49ers’ possibility of signing Joey carries more than just professional significance. It also carries a personal touch: the brothers haven’t played together since their high school days. That was in 2012. Their mother, Cheryl Bosa, really hopes to see Joey in a San Francisco 49ers jersey, just like her other son, Nick. Joey is a former Los Angeles Chargers edge defender who represented the Buffalo Bills in 2025. He recorded 5.0 sacks, 5 forced fumbles, 16 quarterback hits, and 9 tackles for loss in 15 games during the 2025 season. He had signed a one-year, $12M contract with the Bills in March 2025. There was no renewal. He didn’t consider a comeback in the 2026 offseason. Nick said that Joey’s more into golf than the NFL. But there was no retirement news either. This leaves the NFL comeback speculation alive and well and doing cyberspace rounds. He was a capable threat in Buffalo last season, and his extensive experience and pass-rushing ability could make him a useful rotational defender if he ever returns to a team that also features his younger brother, Nick. Joey Bosa retirement rumors continue despite NFL interest Across 10 seasons with the Los Angeles Chargers and Buffalo Bills, he recorded 77 sacks and 22 forced fumbles in 122 games. If he could win a Super Bowl alongside his younger brother Nick Bosa, wouldn’t that be the best closing chapter to his NFL career? We can only hope for that to happen. Or maybe he has retired. Can a previously 0-5 squad keep pushing the turnaround and secure their second straight victory? Last week's win over the Indianapolis Colts represented a new wave of promise for the Titans. But in the Browns, Tennessee will face the top team (in a three-way tie) in the AFC North. Cleveland has come on strong, and are coming to Nashville off a 13-10 win over the Baltimore Ravens. In the wake of a long-awaited win, I've got one reason the Titans will beat the Browns, one reason they won't, as well as my own prediction. Will: Robert Saleh's defense takes over again Robert Saleh's defense just had their best performance of the season. Almost single-handedly, the score-stopping unit bottled up the Colts' offense when it mattered. The Titans forced multiple turnovers and forced Daniel Jones to make mistakes through the air. If Tennessee finds a way to win again this week, it will likely be due to a similar performance from the defense. Expect Saleh to send the heat once again after last week's six-sack outing. PFF has the Browns' offensive line ranked all the way down at 26th in the NFL. If the Titans' defensive line can force Deshaun Watson to unsettle in the pocket, we could be in for a similar path to victory for Tennessee. Won't: Browns get young playmakers going Oppositely, with the Titans' offense still operating at an inconsistent level, this game could get out of hand if Cleveland gets their young playmakers going. Tennessee's defense needs to set the tone early. If the Browns come out swinging, and the Titans' offense takes as long as usual to get into any kind of rhythm, the team could be facing another steep halftime deficit. I just don't like their odds to overcome that two weeks in a row, even if this game is in Nashville. Prediction: Titans win, 17-14 However, I don't believe the Titans will have to worry about that. I'll err to to the positive side with my prediction (something I could be accused of doing too often) and say that Saleh's defense has another big game on the way to a Titans win. This team hasn't won two straight games since Weeks 10 and 11 of the 2022 season. That's a vile streak, but after last week's victory, now feels like the perfect time for Tennessee to break it. Saleh finally has his legs under him as a head coach with this team. The Browns haven't scored more than 13 points in two weeks. picks.blurb: 3 Bold predictions for the Browns against the Titans in Week 7 - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Lendeborg shades Luka Canes' murky ACC future Reese, Dream win Game 3 Ant spoils Giannis' Heat debut World Series preview 3 Bold predictions for the Browns against the Titans in Week 7 Andrew Harbaugh, Browns Wire Wed, October 21, 2026 at 2:55 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Cleveland Browns march into Week 7 with an AFC North division lead and momentum behind them again. They are starting a softer stretch of the schedule but remain focused on the task ahead, which is the Tennessee Titans. Despite winning their first game in Week 6, the Titans are better than they have played. The Browns can win this game, though, if they keep up their defensive aggressiveness and make significant second-half adjustments. Todd Monken and his staff have risen to the occasion in every game, but this could be their first complete game in 2026 if they execute the way they are capable of. We said this is a poor Titans team, but there is still a game to be played, and we have some bold predictions to share ahead of it. Jared Verse gets his first sack of the season This is a wild thing to think about, but heading into Week 7 against the Tennessee Titans, Jared Verse is without a sack this season. Equally, Myles Garrett has also gone without a sack, but he has been on injured reserve. Fair or unfair, Verse is going to be linked to Garrett, and that means expectations will always be high. The Titans' offensive line is not the best unit, they are going to give up pressures, and it is time for Verse to capitalize on that. Jerry Jeudy finds the endzone Jerry Jeudy has seen him get more and more reps and big-time targets since Week 4 against the Pittsburgh Steelers. In Week 6, he made a pivotal catch-and-run that set up the game-winning field goal by Andre Szmyt. Deshaun Watson and Todd Monken have spoke highly of Jeudy this past week and he seems poised for another boost to his role. In Week 7 against he Titans, he can take advantage of their poor secondary and find the endzone for the first time this season. Browns secure at least five sacks Titans quarterback Cam Ward has had a rough start to the season and it has Tennessee sitting with a record of 1-5. He has a tendency to hold onto the ball, be reckless with it, and I think that has the Browns poised to have a big week on the defensive side of the ball. You cannot always count on turnovers, but you can count on Mike Rutenberg being aggressive on defense. One way he will do that is by getting after Ward, and I think that is where the Browns are most productive in the form of securing at least five sacks. away.headline: Injuries cloud Browns-Ravens showdown for AFC North lead in Cleveland
away.blurb: Browns beat reporter Mary Kay Cabot laid out the scope of the problem plainly. “The Ravens have 21 on their injury report today on Thursday, and the Browns have 17,” she said. “The Ravens had two more added today, including Zay Flowers, who was limited with a toe injury. We still don’t even know if Lamar Jackson is playing in this game and we certainly know that there are plenty of Browns that are still idle, still ailing and not sure they’re going to play.” Still, there’s reason to think at least some of those names could return by Sunday. Schwesinger finished last week’s Jets game. Labbe noted that Schwesinger and Graham are “two guys that wouldn’t shock me if we walked out there (Friday) morning and they’re both in the stretch lines getting ready to go.” CLEVELAND, Ohio — 38 players. Two injury reports. Zero certainty about who will actually suit up Sunday when the Browns host the Ravens at Huntington Bank Field with first place in the AFC North on the line. That’s the impossible situation both teams — and anyone trying to analyze this game — find themselves in heading into one of the biggest divisional matchups of the young NFL season. The Browns’ injury list includes defensive cornerstones Carson Schwesinger, Mason Graham and Mike Hall — none of whom had practiced through Thursday. For a defense that’s been Cleveland’s identity all season, those aren’t small absences. Browns beat reporter Ashley Bastock zeroed in on what the late-week practice absences actually mean in practical terms. “It’s always a little concerning when you get to Thursday and they haven’t been on the practice field at all because that does become a really tight turnaround,” she said. “And I think ultimately it’s why we’re going into picking this game, really just having no clue what to do or what’s going to decide it, because it’s really hard to know those things when you don’t know who’s actually going to be on the field.” The Browns have shown real depth this season. Backup defenders Adin Huntington and Sam Kamara performed well against the Jets even without a full complement of starters. But there’s a ceiling to how much depth can compensate. As Labbe put it: “Your starters and your stars are starters and stars for a reason. And eventually, if you don’t have those guys, that can catch up to you.” The Ravens face their own uncertainty — a reshuffled offensive line, Flowers’ toe injury and a quarterback who hasn’t practiced all week. Friday’s practice will be the key for both rosters. Whatever happens, Sunday’s game may ultimately be decided less by scheme than by which injury report clears up first. ©2026 Advance Local Media LLC. Visit cleveland.com. away.headline: Browns new star RB trade target emerges amid injury trouble
away.blurb: The Cleveland Browns are having a good start to the season, as they have a 4-2 record and are at the top of the AFC North. With the way the Browns are playing, it is very likely that they will be buyers ahead of the trade deadline. When looking at the Browns’ current roster, it is clear that they should be looking to add a running back. They have been dealing with injury trouble at the position, so it would not be surprising at all if they acquired a running back by the deadline. Due to this, the Browns are now being connected to a notable running back trade candidate. In a recent article for Bleacher Report , Kristopher Knox named the Browns as the top potential suitor for Tennessee Titans running back Tony Pollard. “Running back Tony Pollard is a good support piece for Ward right now, but he’s 29 years old and an impending free agent. He should have a solid trade market, though, as he has four 1,000-yard seasons on his resume and could upgrade several of the backfields that have been impacted by injuries this season,” Knox wrote. “Potential Suitors: Cleveland Browns, Seattle Seahawks.” Pollard would certainly be an interesting running back for the Browns to add to their roster as they continue their playoff push. The eight-year NFL veteran would provide Cleveland’s offense with a nice boost, as he is still an impactful player at this stage in his career. In six games this season with the Titans, Pollard has recorded one touchdown, 87 rushes, and 349 rushing yards. He also recorded over 1,000 rushing yards over his previous four seasons. With this, the Pro Bowler would be a significant pickup for the Browns if acquired. It will be interesting to see if they pursue him because of it. away.headline: Denzel Boston limited at Cleveland Browns practice with injury
away.blurb: The 6-foot-4 pass catcher was still able to practice in a limited capacity, which is a good sign for his availability on Sunday when the Browns take on the Baltimore Ravens. The second-round pick in April's draft leads the NFL with 20.6 yards per reception, while his 330 yards and 3 touchdowns are the best among all rookies. Boston has tallied 16 catches through the first five games of the year and has been a big part of the Browns starting the season at 3-2, which has them tied for second place in the AFC North. However, after pulling in 3 catches for 46 yards and a touchdown against the New York Jets, Boston popped up on Cleveland's injury report on Wednesday with a foot issue. Throughout the year, Boston has made an early impression on the NFL, displaying why he was such a key piece of Jedd Fisch's offense in the head coach's first two seasons on Montlake. "Not making things too big, just keeping the main thing the main thing," Boston said of his poise and early success . "And also just understanding the camaraderie that we built around the building, having the trust that he's going to go make that play or he's going to go make that play. I think it just comes from a great locker room, a brotherhood, and an understanding of everyone's here for their purpose and everyone's going to fulfill their purpose when the time comes." So, if you’re still alive in Survivor heading into Week 7, you deserve a ton of credit. The SI Betting team was banged up in Week 6, as managing editor Peter Dewey came up short with his Colts pick. On the bright side, those of our readers that tailed senior editor Iain MacMlllam, the New England Patriots improved to 19-2 in their last 21 home games against the New York Jets with a victory on Sunday. The Patriots have won three games in a row and are suddenly back in the mix to earn the top seed in the AFC this season. Week 7 doesn’t feature a ton of obvious Survivor spots, as the Houston Texans (9.5-point favorites against the New York Giants), Minnesota Vikings (5.5-point favorites against the Colts) and Rams (5.5-point favorites against the Las Vegas Raiders) are the three teams favored by the most on Sunday. So, Survivor players are going to have to at least consider a closer game to keep themselves alive. Here’s a quick recap of the Week 6 picks before we share our Week 7 selections. Odds via DraftKings Sportsbook NFL Week 7 Survivor Pool Picks New York Jets Geno Smith and the New York Jets are off to a 2-4 start, but they’ve been competent so far this season. Not only are the Jets 4-1-1 against the spread, but they rank sixth in the NFL in opponent yards per play and are 10th in EPA/Play on defense. The offense isn’t nearly as good (19th in EPA/Play, 22nd in yards per play), but the Jets have a very favorable matchup against a winless Miami Dolphins team – at home – in Week 7. They’ll be returning to U.S. Bank Stadium in Week 7 to host the Indianapolis Colts, and the folks who get paid to set the betting odds seem to think that they’ll emerge from that game unscathed. Our friends from the FanDuel Sportsbook have opened the betting lines for Week 7 in the NFL, and the Vikings are starting the week as a 5.5-point favorite over the Colts. The over/under for this one has started out at 42.5 points. The Colts had a bit of a rough week in Week 6, as they fell to the Tennessee Titans at Lucas Oil Stadium by a score of 26-20. It was the first victory of the season for the Titans, and the Colts couldn’t get out of their own way all afternoon. They turned the ball over three times, including a pair of interceptions from Daniel Jones, and also had a punt that was blocked by the Titans and returned for a touchdown. That’s how the Colts managed to lose despite holding the Titans to just 186 yards of total offense while blowing a 13-0 halftime lead on their home field. That loss dropped the Colts to 2-4 on the season and has our friends from Stampede Blue calling for their team to “ blow it up .” The Vikings, as we’ve mentioned, are one of three teams in the NFL who are still undefeated at 5-0, along with the Kansas City Chiefs and the San Francisco 49ers. The Chiefs climbed to 5-0 by beating the Los Angeles Chargers on Sunday, while the Niners can get to 6-0 if they defeat the Washington Commanders on Monday Night Football. The Vikings have done this despite being fairly anemic on offense, thanks to the performance of their defensive and special teams units. In their last game, they overcame two red zone turnovers to defeat the New Orleans Saints by a score of 23-13 in a game that they played without left tackle Christian Darrisaw and wide receiver Jordan Addison, and saw tight end T.J. Hockenson go out on the second play of the game with a concussion. The sportsbooks have spoken, folks, and the Vikings are pretty significant favorites to push their record to 6-0 this week when they face off against the Colts. away.headline: Colts key playmaker remains sidelined with injury
away.blurb: The Indianapolis Colts are coming off their second-straight and fourth total loss of the 2026 season, and it’s safe to say a large reason why is because they were without one of their top playmakers. Unfortunately, his return to the field remains unknown. The Colts selected Warren with the No. 14 overall pick in the 2025 NFL Draft out of Penn State, where he won the John Mackey Award as the nation’s top tight end in 2024. Related Articles Bears React to NFL Announcement for QB Caleb Williams Following His Return According to Myles Simmons of Pro Football Talk, Colts second-year tight end Tyler Warren was still sidelined on Wednesday with a groin injury. It’s certainly not the news Colts fans were hoping to hear as the team is schedule to take on the undefeated Minnesota Vikings in Week 7. However, head coach Shane Steichen did provide a bit of a promising update after practice. “He’s progressing really well, but I’ll defer to the injury report this week on a lot of those guys,” Steichen said . It can’t be understated how much Warren means to the Colts’ offense. Despite missing Week 6, he still leads the team with 30 catches to go along with 213 yards and two touchdowns. In the meantime, the Colts will have to continue relying on veteran wide receivers Josh Downs, Keenan Allen and Laquon Treadwell as well as backup tight end Mo Alie-Cox. It didn’t take Warren long to establish himself as one of the best up-and-coming tight ends in the league, either. As a rookie, Warren racked up 76 catches for 817 yards and four touchdowns. away.headline: Colts' Week 6 injury report gives fans every reason to expect a Titans win
away.blurb: The Indianapolis Colts must feel pretty good about their health because they released Darius Slayton even though the team has struggled with wide receiver injuries this season. Not so much in Week 6, even though Ashton Dulin (hamstring) is going to be out and Alec Pierce still is . The positive is that Indy has a bye week, also known as having a matchup against the Tennessee Titans. As for Alec Pierce, no timeline exists for when he might return after reinjuring his heel. That might not happen until midseason, and the Colts will probably have far tougher games than the Titans before Pierce comes back. Besides Dulin, the only Indy player who will miss the game, according to head coach Shane Steichen , is linebacker Jaylon Carlies (ribs), but both Carlies and Dulin missed Week 5, and the reason the team lost to the Pittsburgh Steelers had nothing to do with the absences of Dulin and Carlies. The reason was that the defense was terrible again. Therein lies the difference between the Steelers and the Titans, as no matter how bad Indy's defense can be at times, Tennessee doesn't have the offensive talent that Pittsburgh has. Indianapolis Colts should be healthy enough to easily defeat the Tennessee Titans in Week 6 The Titans are 31st in the NFL in yards per play (4.5), last in points scored (58), 28th in quarterback rating (77.2), and 27th in rushing yards per game (82.6). Unless Indianapolis was without defensive lineman DeForest Buckner, cornerbacks Sauce Gardner and Charvarius Ward, and most other good starters, Indianapolis should be able to outscore Tennessee easily. And Buckner, Ward, and Gardner are healthy and will play in Week 6. The Titans haven't beaten Indianapolis since October 2022, a stretch of six straight wins for the Colts, and Indy has no excuse for not making that seven straight victories at Lucas Oil Stadium on Sunday. Injuries won't be a problem for the Colts, at least heading into the game. Tennessee won't have starting safety Kevin Winston Jr., but otherwise they are mostly healthy. They just don't have a lot of talent. They haven't defeated any AFC South team since January 2024, and if that changes against the Colts in Week 6, Indianapolis needs to make some immediate changes. Ultimately, Sunday should be a get-healthy game for the Indianapolis Colts as far as record and standing in the division. When all else is going on, at least Indianapolis can count on two wins every season against the dismal Tennessee Titans . Gardner left the game during Tennessee’s opening possession of the second half after experiencing discomfort in his left leg. According to ESPN’s Stephen Holder, Gardner requested to leave the field before trainers began examining his left calf. The two-time All-Pro was subsequently taken to the locker room for further evaluation. The Colts held a 13-3 lead when Gardner exited during the third quarter. Gardner’s injury raises concerns for Colts defense Gardner eventually returned to the sideline and attempted to loosen up his injured leg, although his availability for the remainder of the contest remained uncertain. Cam Taylor-Britt replaced Gardner at outside cornerback, leaving Indianapolis without its top defensive back. The injury is particularly concerning because Gardner previously experienced calf problems during the 2025 season. Those issues forced him to miss several games after joining Indianapolis in a blockbuster trade with the New York Jets . The Colts surrendered two first-round draft selections and wide receiver Adonai Mitchell to acquire Gardner, demonstrating their commitment to strengthening the secondary. Gardner entered Sunday’s matchup having appeared in all six games this season. According to Colts Wire, opposing quarterbacks had completed nine of 17 passes targeting Gardner for 195 yards, while the veteran cornerback recorded three pass breakups. His ability to match up against opposing receivers makes him an important part of Indianapolis’ defensive strategy. Losing Gardner for an extended period could force the Colts to make significant adjustments in coverage, particularly against teams featuring explosive passing attacks. However, the immediate concern is determining the severity of his latest injury. With Indianapolis looking to remain competitive in the AFC South, keeping its defensive playmakers healthy will be critical. He has also recorded 13 carries for 105 yards (8.1 avg.) and one touchdown. Hardman Jr. has collected 15 kickoff returns for 334 yards (22.3 avg.) and seven punt returns for 86 yards (12.3 avg.). He won Super Bowls LIV and LVIII with the Chiefs. Hardman Jr. was originally selected by Kansas City in the second round (56th overall) of the 2019 NFL Draft out of Georgia. As a rookie, he was an Associated Press Second Team All-Pro choice (kick returner) and was named to the Pro Bowl (return specialist). His first name is pronounced MUH-cole. Morstead, 6-4, 225 pounds, has played in 272 career games in his time with the San Francisco 49ers (2025), New York Jets (2023-24, 2021), Miami Dolphins (2022), Atlanta Falcons (2021) and New Orleans Saints (2009-20). He has registered 1,004 punts for 46,863 yards (46.7 avg./41.3 net avg.) with 374 pinned inside the 20-yard line. Morstead has also totaled 263 touchbacks on kickoffs. He has appeared in 18 postseason contests and has compiled 64 punts for 2,821 yards (44.1 avg./40.8 net avg.) with 22 pinned inside the 20-yard line. Morstead has tallied 16 touchbacks on kickoffs. He won Super Bowl XLIV with New Orleans. Morstead was originally selected by the Saints in the fifth round (164th overall) of the 2009 NFL Draft out of SMU. In 2012, he was an Associated Press Second Team All-Pro choice and was named to the Pro Bowl. Pancol, 6-3, 205 pounds, was signed to the team's practice squad on September 23, 2026. He spent time with the Jacksonville Jaguars during the 2025 offseason program and training camp after originally signing with the team as an undrafted free agent on April 28, 2025, out of Duke. home.blurb: LP = Limited participant in practice. DNP = Did not participate in practice. Probable = the league defines a Probable injury designation as a 75% or greater chance of playing. Historically, 95% of players designated probable are active and played on game day. Questionable = the league defines a Questionable injury designation as being 'uncertain' of whether the player will play or not. This replaces the former definition of having a 50% chance of playing. Historically, 70-75% of players with a Questionable injury designation were active and played on game day. Doubtful = The league defines a Doubtful injury designation to mean the player is unlikely to participate in the game. In practical terms, teams use the designation when a player has less than a 50% chance to suit up, and active game appearances from this designation remain rare. Historically only around 6% of players with a Doubtful designation are active and played on game day. Out = will not play. Players with this designation are not active on game day and league rules prohibit them from playing. For the Colts, they have seven starters who did not practice Wednesday due to injury. They include linebacker Bryce Boettcher, cornerback Sauce Gardner, right guard Matt Gonglaves, punter Rigoberto Sanchez, right tackle Jalen Travis, slot cornerback Justin Walley, and tight end Tyler Warren. Slot Cornerback Justin Walley's injury is new. Not much else is known at this point, but his not practicing and Sauce Gardner already likely out on Sunday could leave the Colts' struggling secondary pretty thin at cornerback. We'll see how it plays out with injury updates tomorrow and Friday. Stowers Sat, October 17, 2026 at 5:47 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Miami's Oct. 25 visit to MetLife Stadium matches two limited offenses and two teams trying to define their seasons. The Jets are early 4.5-point favorites, but the Dolphins' improving rushing attack creates room for several bold predictions. Ollie Gordon II will rush for at least 100 yards. Gordon has totaled 188 yards in two starts since De'Von Achane went on injured reserve. Miami's 217-yard performance against Cincinnati should convince the coaching staff to keep the offense on the ground. New York has been much stronger against the pass than the run, which gives Gordon a favorable path to volume. Malik Willis will produce two touchdowns and no more than one turnover. This is the prediction that would change the game. Willis threw two interceptions and lost a fumble against Cincinnati, but the bye gives Miami time to reduce his difficult reads. Designed runs and play-action can turn his mobility into production while limiting risky throws. Miami will record at least three sacks. The Dolphins have only four sacks through five games, making this the boldest defensive call. Hafley's staff has two weeks to design pressure packages against Geno Smith. A healthier edge rotation and more aggressive use of linebackers could finally create the disruption missing against Cincinnati. The game will be decided by three points or fewer. The early total sits below 40 at several books. New York averages 18.6 points and Miami 14. The Jets have the stronger defense, while the Dolphins have the more productive recent running game. Neither team has shown enough passing explosiveness to create confidence in a runaway. A reasonable projection is Jets 20, Dolphins 17, but that margin leaves the upset door open. If Miami wins the turnover battle, Gordon controls the tempo and special teams avoid another disastrous start, the Dolphins can reverse the score. Bold predictions are not promises. They are matchup-based possibilities. The first three require Miami to emerge from the bye with a more disciplined offense and a more creative defense. If those changes appear, the fourth prediction should follow naturally.

Live Simms Unbuttoned Brian Hamilton , Brian Hamilton Doubtful the Miami Dolphins (0-5) climb out of the cellar in the AFC East this season, but if they are going to, it almost has to begin with a win Sunday afternoon at MetLife Stadium against the New York Jets (2-4). For New York, Sunday offers an opportunity to take another step big picture as an organization and in the moment remain on the fringe of the playoff picture. The Jets are certainly far more competitive than they were a season ago but after a loss last weekend to the Patriots and looking at the rest of their schedule, a win Sunday at home against the winless Dolphins is paramount. They will need more from their offense, though, if they are to win as the Jets average just 18.7 points per game. Miami’s offense is scoring an average of 14 points per game but it’s worse than that for the winless Dolphins. Miami has yet to even lead for even a second in any of their five games this season. New York enters the game following a 26-19 loss to the Patriots in Week 6. The Jets fell behind early and could not overcome their mistakes despite another competitive defensive effort. Prior to that defeat, they snapped a four-game losing streak with a 17-12 win over Cleveland, showing the formula they hope to replicate against Miami: strong defense, ball control, and avoiding turnovers. The Dolphins’ most recent outing was a 31-24 loss to Cincinnati on October 11, arguably their most encouraging offensive performance of the season. Miami rallied in the second half and scored 24 points after managing only 46 total points across its previous four games, but defensive breakdowns once again proved costly as the losing streak extended to five games. Quarterback play will be one of the game’s biggest storylines. Veteran Geno Smith has provided stability for the Jets, throwing for 1,336 yards with seven touchdowns and just one interception through six games. While the Jets’ offense has not consistently produced explosive numbers, Smith has protected the football and given New York a chance to win most weeks. Not the same situation in South Beach. Miami’s Malik Willis has been underwhelming. Yes, the skill positions are lacking with the Dolphins, but the long-time Green Bay backup has to be better. Willis has thrown for 849 yards with a mere two touchdowns along with four interceptions. The Dolphins need greater efficiency if they are going to win or even lead a game. The Dolphins swept both meetings in 2025, including a 34-10 victory at MetLife Stadium last December. away.headline: Dolphins QB Malik Willis practices fully despite thumb injury
away.source: The Palm Beach Post on MSN
away.blurb: "Sometimes it's nine out of 11, 10 out of 11 doing the right thing and one person is not, and it'll mess up the whole play," Willis said. "It's not always that evident watching from the outside, but when we get into the film room, 'Okay, that's what we mean when we're like, it's that close.' You know what I mean? It's easy to say. But you guys go by the results and we haven't been proven those." MIAMI GARDENS ― Miami Dolphins quarterback Malik Willis was treated for an injured thumb on his right, throwing hand, but he fully practiced four days before a Week 7 game at the New York Jets . Willis did not throw at a bye week Monday practice that was open to reporters. Willis did not mention the thumb injury when he met with reporters a short time before the first Jets injury report of the week was released. "(Coach Jeff Hafley) just wanted to get us a little rest, and he wanted to get some young guys in there and see how they were progressing through this season," Willis said when asked what he was dealing with. "But, pretty good." Hafley said at the start of the week that Willis would be fine. "He should be good," Hafley said. "I mean, was he dealing with something? Yeah, I mean, we had a bunch of guys after the (Cincinnati) game that were having a Tuesday practice; usually we don't go until Wednesday. So just rested him on that, but I foresee him being good to go." Miami Dolphins injury report includes Malik Willis thumb Willis has said he hasn't been good enough in his first five Dolphins starts. He is 29th in the NFL with a passer rating of 68.4. He has 2 passing touchdowns, 2 rushing touchdowns, 4 interceptions and 5 fumbles. Willis said he balanced football review and rest and recovery during the bye week. What does Willis think about outside of football? "I mean, the Lord, bro," Willis said. "I keep waking up every day. I got an opportunity to come in here and do my job. I have a family that loves me. I have more than enough. I make it to work safe every day, bro. It's a dangerous world. And we just overlook all these things that are blessings. I try not to do that. And at the same time, I hold myself to the highest of standards. And I just try to focus on the process. Am I doing anything in my power? If I make sure the process is right, the results will come." home.headline: Jets Injury Report: Breece Hall Sits, Adonai Mitchell Limited
home.blurb: The Jets injury report for October 21 features Breece Hall sitting out Wednesday’s practice, while Adonai Mitchell and Dylan Parham participated on a limited basis as New York prepares to host the Miami Dolphins. Mitchell’s limited participation gives the Jets another situation to watch as the week unfolds. Asked whether the receiver’s availability would come down to pain tolerance, Glenn confirmed that was a factor. The coach sounded more optimistic about T’Vondre Sweat and Will McDonald. Both were limited, but Glenn said he expected each to be fine. Their participation over the next two days will provide a clearer picture. Glenn also discussed Omar Cooper Jr.’s return from injured reserve and the additional dimension he brings to the passing game. The coach highlighted Cooper’s deep-ball ability alongside his work after the catch. With Mitchell still working back and Hall’s status unsettled, having Cooper available gives the Jets another offensive weapon as they prepare for Miami. Entertainment Entertainment Home ··· Boxing Aaron Glenn left the door open for Hall to progress during the week. The Jets running back is dealing with a quad injury, but Wednesday’s absence does not establish his availability for Sunday. “He won’t practice today, and we’ll see how tomorrow operates to see how he goes during the week,” Glenn said. Glenn praised Hall’s approach to his recovery, saying he has attacked the process with the same intensity he brings to preparing for a game. Getting him back on the practice field would be an encouraging next step, but that remains something to monitor. Wednesday’s participation and injury designations come from the Jets official report . No game statuses have been assigned yet. Adonai Mitchell Working Back, Sunday Still Uncertain “Yeah, I would say that. I would say the pain tolerance deal,” Glenn said. “So again, we’ll see how that goes as the week goes.” Parham is also beginning to work his way back into practice. His progress bears watching as the Jets look to get healthier on offense heading into a division matchup. Mauigoa and Ossai Remain Week-to-Week Glenn described Kiko Mauigoa and Joseph Ossai as week-to-week. Both missed Wednesday’s practice, along with running back Kene Nwangwu. Omar Cooper Jr. Gives the Offense a Lift “I don’t want to say that it surprised me, but it was just good to see that we have another weapon back and doing the things that we expect him to do,” Glenn said. Thursday’s practice should offer the next meaningful update, particularly on Hall and whether Mitchell can increase his workload. away.headline: Buccaneers vs. Steelers: Final injury report for Week 6
away.blurb: The Tampa Bay Buccaneers have released their final injury report ahead of Sunday's Week 6 matchup against the Pittsburgh Steelers, and several key players will be unavailable as Tampa Bay looks to build on last week's victory over Dallas. Quarterback Baker Mayfield (right thumb) has officially been ruled out after missing all three practices this week. Rookie Jalon Daniels will make his third consecutive start after leading the Buccaneers to their first victory of the season last Thursday against the Cowboys. The Buccaneers will also be without safety Antoine Winfield Jr. (rib), who did not participate in practice throughout the week. Wide receiver David Sills V (hamstring) was also ruled out despite being listed as a full participant in all three practices. Cornerback Benjamin Morrison (quad) is listed as doubtful, while linebackers SirVocea Dennis (ankle/foot) and Josiah Trotter (knee), cornerback Ayden Garnes (ankle), and running back Sean Tucker (quad) are questionable. Dennis and Garnes were full participants Friday, providing some encouraging news heading into the weekend. Pittsburgh is also dealing with several injuries, particularly at wide receiver. Roman Wilson (finger) and Ben Skowronek (calf) have been ruled out, along with safety DeShon Elliott (knee). Wide receiver DK Metcalf was added to Friday's report with an illness and is questionable.
