home.headline: Injuries threw Panthers rookie CB Will Lee III into deep end. Now, he's just 'trying to eat'
home.blurb: The Philadelphia Eagles put that moniker to the test Sunday, when Lee often matched up against DeVonta Smith, a 2021 top-10 pick and Heisman Trophy winner out of Alabama. Though Smith caught a touchdown against Lee in the fourth quarter of Carolina's 25-14 win, the 2026 fourth-round pick finished with six tackles and three pass breakups, becoming the first Carolina rookie with three passes defensed in a game since Keith Taylor in 2021. "It was a great matchup. He's a great receiver, Heisman winner, wide receiver one over there in Philly. And he's a great guy to compete against," Lee said. "That's my big thing. I love competing. I don't care who it is out there, I'm gonna go out there and give it my all." "Talk about Will Lee and the way that he was challenging their best receiver or whoever they put out in front. He got some penalties called on him, but he was in the mix, and he was right there at the top of coverage," Canales said. "He could be a little cleaner with his hands, but I'm not going to back Will Lee off of playing that style of football. I thought that was excellent." The 6-1, 195-pound Lee was known for his strong man coverage skills at Kansas State, where he played in 2023, and Texas A&M, where he spent his final two college seasons. He developed a reputation for being physical and handsy at both stops, not unlike the scouting report on Horn after the Panthers drafted him with the No. 8 pick out of South Carolina in 2021. "I'm a juco guy. I'm grimy. I like to play physical. It's all love at the end of the day, but I'm a competitive person," he said. "I feel like you're out there to embarrass me, and I'm out there to stop you from doing what you're supposed to do. I'm trying to eat, so that's my goal." "He said it's just like repetition. You've gotta learn and feel out the game when you're out there. Some refs are gonna call it different than others, and you've just gotta play the game," Lee said. "He just said be confident in yourself out there and your technique, and you're gonna be just fine." "His demeanor is that of a veteran," Scott said. "A lot of times when you're out there as a young guy, you might have to keep them from being up and down with the result of the drive or the play, giving up a big catch or getting a PBU. They kind of ride that wave. But Will, for the most part, is pretty steady, which definitely makes it easier on everybody." Now, Jackson's status for Week 7 is up in the air, though oddsmakers have set the Ravens as three-point favorites at home in their matchup with the Cincinnati Bengals. DraftKings Sportsbook has Baltimore set at -148 to win this game, a sign that oddsmakers are bracing for Jackson to return from his two-game absence. After Jackson was ruled out for Week 6, Ravens head coach Jesse Minter gave a rather vague update on the star quarterback's status. "It's day by day, I would say," Minter said ahead of Week 6. "And I think it's just a decision for his best interest. And that's really what every decision's always going to be about." Jackson was injured in the first half of Baltmore's Week 4 win over Tennessee and did not return. He had thrown multiple scores in that game, giving the Ravens a huge cushion and they went on to win with Tyler Huntley at the helm. Huntley then received the start in Week 5 against the Atlanta Falcons and played a really solid game to lead the Ravens to a win. He completed 24 of his 32 pass attempts for 201 yards and two scores and added a touchdown on the ground in an overtime win. At 4-1, the Ravens were in a great spot in the AFC North, and ESPN's Adam Schefter had reported that Jackson has a realistic chance to return in Week 6. However, the two-time MVP did not practice all week ahead of the game against Cleveland, and was eventually ruled out. Huntley struggled to move the offense, throwing for 165 yards and a score in a 13-10 loss. Cleveland is now ahead of the Ravens in the division, and Baltimore wants to avoid a similar fate in Week 7 against Cincinnati. While the Ravens have won three of the last four games Huntley has started in place of Jackson, they are still just 7-12 without the star quarterback all time. It's unlikely that the Ravens would close as favorites, even at home, if Jackson were to miss the game against Joe Burrow and Co. in Week 7. This season, Jackson has completed 70.8 percent of his passes for 967 yards, six scores and just one interception. The Ravens star leads the league in yards per attempt, yards per completion and passer rating in 2026. He also has 19 carries for 144 yards and a score, a sign that his rushing is back to a higher level than it was in 2025. Baltimore's practice reports should give a better look into Jackson's status this week, but bettors should treat him as highly questionable until he is able to return to the practice field. As for the Baltimore Ravens , their kicker is on notice. These teams meet in a Week 7 AFC North clash, and here are bold predictions for the contest. The Bengals (3-2) enter the game in last place in the division despite having a winning record. That's because the Ravens, Steelers, and surprising Browns all have a record of 4-2. It should be another battle for the Ravens and Bengals. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Joe Burrow will riddle the Ravens' defense for 3 TD passes When the Bengals are right, they are tough on offense. And they've been cooking this year, ranking No. 9 in the NFL in points per game. Burrow is connecting on 71.4% of his passes. He has 11 touchdown passes and three interceptions. Look for him to keep the momentum going this week. But Burrow needs to take care of the football, which Zac Taylor said would go a long way in helping the Bengals win, according to Cleveland.com. "The turnovers is what screams at you," Taylor said. "That leads into field position." And Taylor said Burrow and his teammates are ready for this matchup. "It's exciting," Taylor said. "I think our guys really get fired up for this game. Not that they don't get fired up for every game, but whenever we play in Baltimore in a road divisional game, it's a fun one to get up for, and our guys will be up for it." Bengals RB Chase Brown will score two TDs One of them will be on the receiving end of a pass from Burrow. Brown will have a nice day, despite being caught in a time share with Samaje Perine, according to The Athletic. "I think we'll continually assess how that touch share between (Perine) and Chase Brown should play out," Bengals offensive coordinator Pitcher told Geoff Hobson of Bengals.com. "Every game's different. What type of scheme we lean into is going to factor into that. Obviously, what we ran more of yesterday leans into what Samaje does well, which is get downhill and run through contact." The Bengals haven't forgotten about their ground game. "You strive for balance when it comes to run-pass," Pitcher said. "You're always wanting to be the most balanced and versatile version of yourselves. It's like those are high-level goals that you set out to attain. But never in any given situation are we going to let a high-level theoretical goal get in the way of what it means on Sunday to win a game and what is the feedback we're getting in a game on a given Sunday." Derrick Henry will rush for 80-plus yards and a TD Henry is still smarting from last week's fumble that led to the Ravens' loss to the Browns. He took blame for the game-changing turnover , according to ESPN. "I got to take care of the ball," he said. "There's no excuses for that. I got to be better. I put the team in harm's way. I sound like a broken record with this, but I got to go back to work on it. Can't put the team in that situation." Teammate Kyle Hamilton took up for Henry. "Obviously, he's Derrick Henry, Hall of Fame running back [who] wants to hold onto the ball," Hamilton said. "He knows that. He's his harshest critic, so I'm not going to say anything ill about it. He's put us in position to win a lot of games." All of this will motivate Henry for a big game against the Bengals Ravens WR Ja'Kobi Lane will catch 5 passes and score a TD Lane looked ready to roll against the Browns in his return from injury. And he should be able to carve out a significant role in Week 7. Lane looked great in training camp. The injury short-circuited his 2026 season. But now he's back in the mix. His overall stat line could be impacted if Tyler Huntley is still at quarterback. But if Jackson is back, this could be a breakout game for Lane. Who will win the game? The Bengals should be able to outscore the Ravens in this matchup. But the key factor is Jackson. If he's back, the Ravens have a much better chance of winning. But we will still roll with Burrow, Chase, and Tee Higgins having a big game, along with Brown doing his thing. Joe Burrow looking forward to facing Trey Hendrickson Burrow has practiced against Hendrickson many a time over the years, but the two have never been opponents in a real game before. away.blurb: Lamar Jackson returned to the field for Thursday’s practice, giving the Ravens another encouraging development ahead of Sunday’s matchup against Cincinnati. Thursday’s appearance builds on that progress, although his participation level and availability against the Bengals remain to be determined. Before the injury, Jackson completed 68 of 96 passes for 967 yards, six touchdowns and one interception, producing a 119.6 passer rating. He also rushed for 144 yards and a touchdown on 19 carries, averaging 7.6 yards per attempt. Jackson’s return would add a different dimension to an offense seeking more consistency. His 10.1 yards per pass attempt this season reflects the explosive passing production Baltimore had before his injury. Baltimore has gone 1-1 in his absence, beating Atlanta in overtime before falling 13-10 at Cleveland. Tyler Huntley completed 19 of 31 passes for 165 yards and a touchdown against the Browns, but the Ravens went scoreless over the final three quarters. The Ravens host a rested Bengals team Sunday with another important division result at stake. Thursday’s official injury report and Jackson’s response to the increased workload will clarify whether he can make his first appearance since Week 4. However, coach Jesse Minter said after practice that Jackson got some “limited” work and did it with the team rather than individually. Under league rules, that participation could have been limited to the team’s walk-through earlier in the day. He was listed as limited on the injury report. Last year, the NFL fined the Ravens $100,000 after an injury report gaffe involving Jackson. On their final injury report ahead of a Week 8 game against the Chicago Bears, they listed him as a full participant in that day’s practice, even though he only took reps with the scout team, an indication he was not ready to return from his hamstring injury. As for when Jackson will be ready to return from his latest ailment, Minter wouldn’t say for sure. Last season, hamstring and back injuries cost Jackson four games. In 2022, a knee sprain kept him out for the final six regular-season games and a wild-card playoff game. In 2021, he missed one game because of illness and the final four regular-season games with an ankle injury. Going to venerated Wembley Stadium, facing off against the division-leading Jaguars, who had the advantage of having played in England the week prior and didn't have to worry about their body clocks, and managing to get away with a win was huge for the Texans. Houston, now at 2-4 but having won two straight road games against division rivals, returns to NRG Stadium to host the New York Giants of New Jersey. The Giants, sitting at 3-2-1, come into this matchup atop the NFC East, despite not winning in their last two games, a tie at Washington and a loss against New Orleans. In their last game, they fell to the Saints 34-27, but the Saints held a lead of 34-10 at one point in the 4th Quarter. The Giants, forced to start backup QB Jameis Winston since starter Jaxson Dart went down with a season-ending injury, decided to give recent trade acquisition J.J. The New York/New Jersey sports pages will have themselves a field day talking about the QB spot in this coming week. Likely because of that QB uncertainty, along with Houston's recent winning streak and the supposed talent disparity, the opening odds from FanDuel for the upcoming matchup between the Texans and the Giants are strongly supporting Houston at home: Overall, this may seem a bit high of an opening line. The Giants haven't played as difficult a schedule as Houston and they are coming in with key injuries and roster concerns. However, the Texans, even coming off a huge win against Jacksonville, are still struggling on defense and sit at 0-3 at home. They have only beaten the Giants once in 6 total meetings, and that was in 2002. Sandwiched between an international game and a bye week, this has the feel of a trap game for Houston. This particular line may tighten a bit as the week progresses, especially as the Giants sort out their QB situation and both teams sort out their respective injury situations. away.headline: Breaking down the Saints-Giants injury report: Who's in, who's out?
away.blurb: Breaking down the Saints-Giants injury report: Who's in, who's out? - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Breaking down the Saints-Giants injury report: Who's in, who's out? We're breaking down the final New Orleans Saints injury report for Week 6's road game against the New York Giants . Who's in, who's out, and who has a chance to play? The Giants ruled out safety Tyler Nubin (neck), tight end Theo Johnson (neck), and cornerback Colton Hood (concussion). WR Chris Olave (illness) didn't practice on Wednesday or Thursday, but he was able to work on a limited basis during Friday's practice. He should play so long as that illness is behind him. DL Nathan Shepherd (illness) also missed two days of practice with an illness that's been going around the locker room. He was limited on Friday as well. CB Lorenzo Styles Jr. (knee) was limited on both Thursday and Friday, so don't be surprised if he's a game-time decision. RB Alvin Kamara (back) practiced on limited reps throughout the week. The Saints didn't bring up either of the two running b acks on their practice squad so it does llook like he'll play. Starting offensive linemen Andrew Thomas (groin) and Jermaine Eluemunor (calf) are both questionable for the Giants, as is edge rusher Abdul Carter (calf). There's a crowd of Giants players available to play after being listed on the injury report this week: cornerback Greg Newsome II (groin), outside linebacker Malik Harrison (groin), defensive back Elijah Campbell (thumb), running back Najee Harris (ribs), tight end Isaiah Likely (foot), wide receivers Darnell Mooney (neck) and Charlie Jones (Achilles), as well as safety Jason Pinnock (concussion). As was the case last week, the following Saints players are on injured reserve with season-ending injuries: defensive tackle Bryan Bresee, running back Ty Chandler, cornerback David Long Jr., tight end Moliki Matavao, offensive lineman Dillon Radunz, and cornerback Rejzohn Wright. However, a couple of others have been designated to return after sitting out at least four games: rookie wide receiver Jordyn Tyson and veteran running back Travis Etienne Jr. are both expected to return after the bye week in November but it sounds like we won't see left tackle Kelvin Banks Jr. until December at the soonest. Offensive lineman Nick Saldiveri is on the season-ending PUP list (physically unable to perform), while wide receiver Mason Tipton is eligible to return after missing four games. Tipton has not returned to practice yet. This article originally appeared on Saints Wire: Breaking down the Saints-Giants injury report: Who's in, who's out? away.blurb: Thomas, who has sat out Wednesday and Thursday over the past several weeks and returned to practice on a limited basis on Friday and Saturday before being cleared to play, is someone to watch this week. Last week he came out of the game just before the big fourth-quarter comeback attempt against the Saints; the veteran left tackle was visibly laboring through his groin injury throughout the game. Starting safety Jevon Holland was spotted at practice, off to the side with a trainer. Newsome and Holland have been the Giants defensive secondary’s best players so far this season, so hopefully their absences aren’t serious enough to keep them out of Sunday’s game. Speaking of the cornerback position, Newsome did not practice, but rookie Colton Hood (concussion) did. Sills, 6-foot-6 and 325 pounds, was originally an undrafted free agent out of Oklahoma State whom the Eagles signed in 2022. That season, Sills, who has played guard in his short NFL career, was one of three undrafted free agents to make the Eagles roster but only appeared in one game for Philadelphia. Giants Injury Report: Giants O-line Thinned By Injuries Skip to main content SI.COM The New York Giants will face one of the best defenses on Sunday when they travel to Houston to meet the Texans. So it was a bit alarming that on Wednesday, the team’s top three offensive tackles were not practicing. Starters Andrew Thomas (groin), Jermaine Eluemunor (calf), and swing tackle Marcus Mbow (knee) were not participating in practice during the media viewing period. Eluemunor missed last week’s game as well with his injury after saying he would test it to see if he could anchor; he is also someone to watch this week. And with MBow now nursing something, the Giants could be thin at offensive tackle if he can’t play. The Texans have league sack leader Will Anderson, Jr. on one side of their formation and Danielle Hunter on the other. That would be quite the test for rookie J.C. Davis, who would presumably play left tackle; at right tackle, the Giants could potentially move Sisi Mauigoa from right guard to tackle, the position he played in college. Edmunds, Newsome Not Spotted During Media Viewing Portion of Practice Inside linebacker Tremaine Edmunds (shoulder) and cornerback Greg Newsome II (concussion) were not spotted at practice during the media viewing portion. If Edmunds can’t go, Micah McFadden would get the start. The question then becomes who would wear the radio in his helmet: rookie Arvell Reese, the most likely candidate, or someone else. Rookie Colton Hood (concussion), receiver Darnell Mooney (neck), safety Tyler Nubin (neck), and tight end Theo Johnson (neck) were spotted at practice during the media viewing portion. Paulson Adebo’s Practice Window Opens Cornerback Paulson Adebo’s 21-day practice window is now open. If he clears, he could fill the roster vacancy left after Tuesday’s release of running back Najee Harris and defensive lineman Jihad Ward. Adebo has been on IR since Week 2

home.blurb: Texans WR Tank Dell to return from gruesome 2024 knee injury on Sunday vs. Giants - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL "I don't have any expectations, I'm just happy to see him out there," Ryans said, via ESPN Radio's Will Kunkel . Dell ended up tearing multiple ligaments , sustained meniscus damage and dislocated his left knee in the incident. It knocked him out of the entire 2025 campaign, and he's been recovering ever since. Dell had 667 receiving yards and three touchdowns in 14 games during the 2024 campaign. The Texans selected him in the third round of the 2023 NFL Draft out of Houston. Though it's unclear if Dell will be able to compete at the same level he was at previously, considering how significant his knee injury and rehab actually was, he's finally ready to get back out onto the field. The next part of his playing career is here. Ant spoils Giannis' Heat debut Ryan Young Staff writer Mon, October 19, 2026 at 8:13 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads The Houston Texans wide receiver will take the field on Sunday for their matchup with the New York Giants, head coach DeMeco Ryans confirmed on Monday. It will mark Dell's first game back since he went down with a gruesome knee injury in 2024. Dell caught a deep pass from quarterback C.J. Stroud in a matchup with the Kansas City Chiefs in December 2024. But as Dell was bringing the ball in, teammate Jared Wayne dove for the ball too and accidentally crashed into Dell's left knee. Dell made the catch, and completed the 30-yard touchdown, but the injury was gruesome. He had to be driven off the field on a stretcher in what was a very emotional scene at Arrowhead Stadium. He remained in a Kansas City-area hospital overnight, and returned to Houston the next day. The injury was just the latest significant one that Dell has already faced in his career. His rookie season was cut short after he fractured his fibula just 11 games in, and he was then shot in the leg as a bystander at a mass shooting in Florida in 2024. Dell recovered from both injuries in time to start the 2024 campaign normally. Dell will rejoin the Texans at a critical time for the organization this season, too. After losing four straight to start the year, they've now won back-to-back contests entering Sunday's matchup with the Giants at NRG Stadium. They most recently rallied to beat the Jacksonville Jaguars in London on Sunday.

home.headline: DeMeco Ryans Announces Reed Blankenship Injury Status After Houston Texans’ Win
home.blurb: The Houston Texans finally had a reason to celebrate after Ka'imi Fairbairn's last-second field goal sealed a 34-31 win over the Jacksonville Jaguars in London. But the victory also came with concerns for a defense that had struggled to meet expectations this season. Safety Reed Blankenship left the game with a concussion, and coach DeMeco Ryans gave an update on his condition ahead of Sunday's matchup against the New York Giants. Another starting safety, Jalen Pitre, also remained uncertain to return as Houston prepared for Week 7. Blankenship had to clear the NFL's concussion protocol when Ryans spoke to reporters on Tuesday, October 21. The safety suffered the injury in the second quarter against Jacksonville while attempting to tackle running back Chris Rodriguez Jr. He could not return to the game, leaving Houston to prepare for its next matchup without knowing whether he would be available. The coach addressed Pitre, who missed the London game with a shoulder injury. His recovery had shown some progress, but Houston had not set a return date. “Seven key Texans players did not practice Wednesday as they began preparations for Sunday's game against the Giants. Linebacker Azeez Al-Shaair (knee), safety Reed Blankenship (concussion/hand), offensive tackle Trent Brown (wrist), offensive tackle Blake Fisher (thumb), running back David Montgomery (groin), safety Jalen Pitre (shoulder) and tight end Dalton Schultz (quad) spent the day rehabbing,' Charean Williams of Pro Football Talk wrote. The criticism wasn't limited to his coverage numbers. HTX Sports' Clayton Anderson questioned whether Houston should reconsider Blankenship's role if the secondary performed better without him.Then again, the team's defensive struggles are not limited to one player. Pitre's absence also left Houston without another starter, and his shoulder injury had become a recurring concern. The Texans now faced the New York Giants on Sunday, with a hope of a London victory. Where Blankenship's availability was not unresolved, while Tank Dell was expected to return after nearly two years away from a serious knee injury. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images Ian St. Clair Wed, October 21, 2026 at 1:00 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Bo Nix and the Denver Broncos are coming off a huge win over the defending Super Bowl champs. Next on the docket is a scrappy Arizona Cardinals bunch that just pulled a huge road upset of the Los Angeles Rams. The good news for the Broncos (4-2) is that they got the mini-bye week before heading to the desert and could get a few players back from injury and the commissioner's exempt list. Denver looks to extend its winning streak to three games after coming out of a gauntlet to start the season. The Broncos are currently -4.5-point road favorites over Arizona (2-4). The total sits at over/under 43.5 points, with a lean toward the over at -115. Offensive Rankings Denver : Thirty-first in total offense (252.2 yards per game), 26th in rushing offense (84.2 YPG), 28th in passing offense (168.0 YPG), 26th in scoring offense (19.0 points per game). Arizona : Twenty-third in total offense (307.3 yards per game), 22nd in rushing offense (96.3 YPG), 20th in passing offense (211.0 YPG), 24th in scoring offense (21.0 points per game). Defensive Rankings Denver : Twenty-second in total defense (348.3 yards per game), 31st in rushing defense (139.8 YPG), 10th in passing defense (208.5 YPG), tied for 10th in scoring defense (20.8 points per game). Arizona : Twenty-third in total defense (350.5 yards per game), 20th in rushing defense (120.8 YPG), 22nd in passing defense (229.7 YPG), tied for 31st in scoring defense (29.7 points per game). Here are the MHR staff's keys to Sunday's game. Win the line of scrimmage on offense The Broncos offensive line has been the definition of "meh" to start the regular season. It's nowhere near what it's been the last few seasons, but it also isn't horrid either. Denver needs to dominate the line of scrimmage on Sunday. Open lanes in the running game and do a better job of pass protection. It's a cliche, but success on offense starts in the trenches. Getting that could lay the foundation for jump-starting the offense. — Ian St. Clair Bench Bo Nix; Start Jarrett Stidham Just kidding. Ya'll crazy if you think benching Bo Nix is even remotely the answer. That said, Bo Nix does need to play better, and he isn't seeing the field well to start the season. He's had slow starts in every season he's played, so, for now, I'm chalking this up to another slow start. However, seven games in, I'm hoping to see him take flight a bit now that the hardest part of the Broncos' schedule is complete. At 4-2, they got through it with a winning record, and that is all we could hope for. — Tim Lynch Pressure the QB The key to this game is the same as it has been every week. Get to the QB. The defense has done a great job this season of causing mayhem in the backfield. Make it uncomfortable for Jacoby Brissett (like the back of a Volkswagen). When QBs are harassed and hurried, they make mistakes. — Adam Malnati Disciplined, execution-based offensive football This team needs to execute at a high level, and it will win this game easily. The defense is already there. If the offense can up its game, this Broncos team will be unstoppable. — Sadaraine Limit the impact of Trey McBride The Broncos defense has performed well this season, aside from a few games. For the most part, they've been able to limit the impact of the opposing team's top player on their offense. This week, they face All-Pro tight end Trey McBride, who is coming off a sensational 2025 season. He is the focal point of Arizona's aerial attack and gets over ten targets per game. Defensive coordinator Vance Joseph needs to come up with a good game plan that limits his impact on the game. If they can slow him down, Denver will have a great shot at earning their fifth victory of the season. — Christopher Hart What are your keys to Sunday's game?

away.headline: Latest Broncos' injury report indicates key players are nearing a return
away.blurb: Running back Jonah Coleman, who has been designated to return from IR with his ankle injury, practiced in full on Wednesday. Patrick Surtain II, who left the team's Week 4 game with an ankle injury, was also at practice on a limited basis: Unfortunately, Tyler Badie, Talanoa Hufanga, and Jonah Elliss all did not practice, and Elliss' injury could end up being more extended. Hufanga hurt his ankle in Week 5 against the Los Angeles Chargers, and both Badie and Elliss got hurt in Week 6 against the Seattle Seahawks. Fortunately, Hufanga's injury is minor. As for Surtain, James Palmer is reporting that the likely return for the Defensive Player of the Year is Week 8 against Kansas City, but he also didn't totally shut the door on Surtain playing this week : Him practicing in limited fashion does give him a chance to play, but you almost want to wonder if the Broncos understand the opponents they have coming up and want to ease Surtain back into things for Week 8, as that game could carry major impact across the division and conference in terms of seeding. All in all, the Broncos seem to be trending toward being more 'full strength' for the Chiefs game in Week 8. However, not only could Coleman find his way back into the lineup in Week 7, but, until he's ruled out, Surtain could be nearing a return as well. The Broncos also have wide receiver Pat Bryant on IR. He is eligible to return f in Week 9 against the Carolina Panthers. Denver plays Arizona, Kansas City, and Carolina before the Week 10 bye, which just so happens to line up nicely with the trade deadline. This article was originally published on predominantlyorange.com as Latest Broncos' injury report indicates key players are nearing a return . The Denver Broncos have dealt with their share of injuries this year, unfortunately. The bright side though, is that the Broncos are consistently among the least-injured teams in the NFL, and the ailments this year have largely been minor. As the middle of the season approaches, the playoff race will slowly start to heat up, and Week 8 against the Kansas City Chiefs could present a legitimate playoff atmosphere. Before the Chiefs, though, the Broncos have to get by the Arizona Cardinals in Week 7. And in the team's first injury report of the week, it does seem to indicate that the team could get some key players back. Pick: Jets 19, Dolphins 17 Tampa Bay Buccaneers (+3.5) at Carolina Panthers The Bucs might have Baker Mayfield back for this one. That would be big. McCarthy , but we will see. No matter who starts, the Texans ' defense is having issues. The Giants will move the ball. But they won't stop C.J. Stroud . Lions win it by a tiny margin as both quarterbacks light it up. The Rams have a lot of injury issues, which have really impacted their team. They still have Matt Stafford. He can light up a defense, which he will do here. But the Rams will give up some big plays to the Raiders , who hang around. picks.blurb: Packers vs. Lions bold predictions for NFC North clash in Week 7 - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Lendeborg shades Luka Canes' murky ACC future Reese, Dream win Game 3 Ant spoils Giannis' Heat debut World Series preview Packers vs. Lions bold predictions for NFC North clash in Week 7 Packers head coach Matt LaFleur with QB Jordan Love with a logo of the Green Bay Packers behind them. Ben Strauss, ClutchPoints Wed, October 21, 2026 at 9:21 PM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The NFC North still looks like one of the NFL's most competitive divisions just six weeks into the 2026 season. Every team in the division finished with a winning record in 2025, and that trend has continued into this year . Now the Packers and Lions are gearing up for a huge divisional matchup that could have huge ramifications come playoff time. Green Bay is looking strong after a questionable start to the season. They are on a three-game winning streak after taking care of Dallas on Sunday Night Football . The Packers are still a bit behind the Vikings, but getting a win in Week 7 will get them one step closer to catching up. Meanwhile, Detroit quieted their doubters in Week 5 after crushing Arizona in the desert. The Lions even got a solid game from their defense, something that has eluded them for most of the season. But Detroit is coming off their bye week, so it is impossible to know if they'll carry over that momentum or come out flat. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Which team will come out on top in this massive divisional matchup? Here are three bold predictions before the NFC North clash between the Lions and Packers in Week 7. Jared Goff throws his first interception of the season, but still shreds Packers defense Mark Konezny-Imagn Images Goff may be the most underrated quarterback in the entire NFL this season. He may look like a quarterback from a different age, but Goff can still sling it with the best of them. Detroit's franchise quarterback has 1,485 passing yards with 12 touchdowns and zero interceptions through five games. That's right, he still has not thrown an interception at any point this season. This speaks to how careful Goff is with the football, no doubt owing to his veteran experience. All of that said, this could be the week that the streak comes to an end. The Lions should not underestimate the Packers' defensive unit, even if they don't have Micah Parsons in Week 7. Green Bay has one of the better coverage units in the NFL this season despite an unproven cornerback room. Even more impressive is that they lead the NFL in interceptions with nine through the first six games. If any team is going to snap Goff's streak, it will be the packers. Goff will throw his first interception of the season against Green Bay on Sunday. All good things must come to an end, including his impressive streak of clean games. However, that doesn't mean he'll wilt against the Packers. Detroit will finish this game with at least 400 passing yards, shredding Green Bay's secondary from wire to wire. Josh Jacobs rumbles for 100 rushing yards, two touchdowns in 2026 debut Green Bay's one weakness this season has been their rushing attack. The Packers are averaging a pitiful 59.8 rushing yards per game this season. That is due to a combination of offensive line issues and a thin running back group. But the latter is about to change. Getting Jacobs back won't fix everything overnight. After all, it is fair to be skeptical of how ready he truly is after staying away from football for over a month. On paper, they're in the same tier as Detroit in terms of passing yards per game. The good news for the Lions is that Brian Branch is expected to make his 2026 debut against the Packers in Week 7. It is impossible to know just how good Branch will look after last season's Achilles injury . Getting him back is also no guarantee that Detroit's defense will magically play better. But it is a start. In the long term, getting Branch back should do wonders for the Lions. Unfortunately, it won't be enough to win this game. picks.headline: Packers vs. Lions predictions: Detroit's biggest weakness could decide Week 7
picks.blurb: Detroit scores points like no other, but also gives them up at an alarming rate. In other words, Christian Watson and Matthew Golden should be salivating at the matchup. The fantasy managers who roster those players will be thinking the same thing. More importantly, this is a key contest in the ever-crowded NFC North where there is no margin for error. Green Bay enters the contest at 4-2, erasing any negative thoughts that surfaced after the 0-2 start to the year. Detroit is 3-2, which is good enough for last place in the NFC North. Both teams are chasing the 5-0 Vikings , with the 4-2 Bears standing in the way as well. With only so many playoff spots to go around, this Week 7 matchup could have massive implications down the road. Here's a look at the keys to the game, injuries to watch and a prediction. Lions vs Packers odds, moneyline, over/under Opening lines: Spread: Lions -2.5 Moneyline: Lions -142; Packers +120 Get the edge with our exclusive NFL betting picks Lions Keys To Victory Slow down Christian Watson and Matthew Golden. It's easier said than done, of course, but it's the one true path to victory for Detroit - outside of winning a shootout. The Lions' secondary has been a huge weakness all season long, and perhaps there is no better team position to exploit that than the Packers. Green Bay will try to hit some home runs with its speedy receivers. Even with Brian Branch set to return, Detroit will have to be willing to sit back in zone coverage and hold the visitors to some singles. Packers Keys To Victory Stay patient. With a defense as weak as the Lions, the Packers just have to play the waiting game. And that's something Dan Campbell's teams haven't been known to do. Detroit can either take away the long ball or attempt to get to Jordan Love with pressure. If the Lions sit back, then the Packers need to show an ability to run the ball. If they pressure, get ready to light up the scoreboard. Green Bay has the advantage, but it can't beat itself. Injuries to watch • S Brian Branch • OL Cade Mays • OL Aaron Banks. Lions vs Packers USA TODAY expert picks Nicholas Brinkerhoff: Packers 34, Lions 30 This game might come down to who has the ball last. Detroit might be coming out of the bye with some reinforcements, but this is still a defense that will ruin a season. And for that reason, no lead is safe - especially against the rival Packers, who can strike quickly. Jordan Love was forced to grow up as a quarterback without a running game to rely on through the first six weeks. He is passing that test with flying colors after a slow start. Trust the more well-rounded Packers to get the job done and push their winning streak to four. Adam Kaufman: Lions 31, Packers 27 This should be fun. Green Bay has won three straight, but Detroit comes out of its bye with reinforcements. Brian Branch's expected return won't magically fix the secondary, though even a few additional stops could make a significant difference. The Lions already have an offense capable of taking advantage, with Jahmyr Gibbs headlining their weapons. Jordan Love should still find opportunities, and the Packers can absolutely win if they protect him and avoid giving the home team extra possessions. Josh Jacobs' availability is another important piece. I'm expecting both quarterbacks to have productive stretches. But Jared Goff and Dan Campbell have been a dynamic duo with extended rest and know what's at stake in a crowded NFC North. This should be competitive well into the fourth quarter, but I like the Lions indoors. away.blurb: Green Bay Packers head coach Matt LaFleur addressed Josh Jacobs’ return Wednesday, acknowledging the running back’s off-field legal troubles while expressing his belief in second chances. For now, the former Alabama standout is eligible to return, but his status for Sunday and potential league discipline remain unresolved. Jacobs returned to practice after missing Green Bay’s first six games while on the NFL’s Commissioner’s Exempt List. His reinstatement comes amid an ongoing league investigation into a domestic incident involving his former girlfriend. The 33rd Team’s Ari Meirov shared a video on X, formerly Twitter, showing LaFleur discussing how the Packers balance welcoming Jacobs back with the seriousness of his legal case. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) The 2022 first-team All-Pro running back pleaded no contest to misdemeanor battery and criminal damage to property charges stemming from a May altercation with his then-girlfriend. Additional discipline remains possible, and whether his six missed games will count toward a future suspension has not been finalized. Jacobs and the woman involved also filed a lawsuit seeking to prevent the release of evidence related to the incident. On the field, the Packers desperately need rushing production. away.blurb: That said, star quarterback Jordan Love was listed as a limited participant due to a back injury. Not only that, but his top wide receivers, Christian Watson and Matthew Golden, were both listed as limited participants as well. Seeing Watson's name on an injury report is never good, knowing what he's dealt with in his career. He was listed as limited due to an ankle injury in this one, while Golden is dealing with an apparent shoulder injury. Offensive guard Aaron Banks was listed as limited due to a knee/toe injury, but thankfully he was the only offensive lineman on the report. Defensively, cornerbacks Brandon Cisse (shoulder/neck) and Benjamin St-Juste (hamstring) were both limited. Defensive tackles Anthony Campbell (ankle) and Jordon Riley (Achilles) were also limited. It should be noted that the Packers didn't officially practice, so these are all just estimations. In the biggest surprise of the week, running back Josh Jacobs didn't see his name on the report, so he should be a full-go in Week 7 against the Detroit Lions. It's not like Love necessarily got obliterated by the Dallas Cowboys, but he was sacked three times, one of which was by his former teammate, Kenny Clark. Love has been sacked 13 times in six games this season, and he also tied his season high with four carries on Sunday Night Football. Green Bay has always been careful about using him in the run game, but they dialed up a perfect zone read against fellow former Packers defender Rashan Gary. This is one of, if not the most dynamic receiving duos in the entire league right now, and each had a big drop or two against the Dallas Cowboys, but the team's confidence in them, specifically Golden, is through the roof.

home.headline: The Detroit Lions have decided on a punt returner to replace Tom Kennedy
home.blurb: After Tom Kennedy suffered a season-ending injury in their last game against the Arizona Cardinals, the Lions will replace him on both punt and kick return with newly signed receiver DeAndre Carter. Special teams coordinator Dave Fipp said they aren’t viewing the job as completely open at this point in the week. “I don’t know that it’s like totally open. I think DeAndre Carter’s got a lot of experience. He’ll probably step in and return punts for us and kickoffs for us in the game, along with (Jacob) Saylors. And we’ll just keep going as it’s been,” Fipp said. Fipp noted that there were players, like Lucky Jackson, who have punt return experience, but it pales in comparison to Carter’s résumé. Carter, who entered the league in 2015, has returned 155 career punts for 1,508 yards (9.7 average) and 144 kickoffs for 3,399 yards (23.6 average). The Detroit Lions aren’t hiding their intentions when it comes to their new punter/kick returner. Carter is currently on the practice squad, so in order to play, he will either sign to the 53-man roster this week or receive a game-day elevation from the practice squad. Carter has had a tumultuous NFL career. Despite entering the league in 2015, he didn’t see the field until 2018. He was rostered by the Ravens, Raiders, Patriots, and 49ers before he played in his first NFL game—ironically with the Philadelphia Eagles and their special teams coach at the time, Dave Fipp. In his first game as punt returner, Carter took a late punt, returned it 42 yards, setting up the Eagles for what would be the game-tying score . Fipp said he’s always had respect for Carter’s resilience and the way he plays the game. “He bounced around, kept on fighting, trying to make it,” Fipp said. “I think we’re in Week 4 or something like that, I believe. It was when Darren Sproles went down. And then he came in, we’re playing against Tennessee, and he did what he does. He catches the ball, he competes, he gets downfield, he’s quick, very competitive. His story is like the ultimate story of just overcoming all the obstacles, and he plays the game that way. He loves playing football. I’ve always respected his game.”

home.blurb: The Green Bay Packers’ star quarterback, who has carried the load for most of the team’s 4-2 start, was deemed limited participation on Wednesday, the first day of on-the-field work before Sunday’s NFC North showdown at the Detroit Lions. Only one player, receiver Bo Melton (back), would not have practiced. Nine players were limited, including Love and receivers Matthew Golden (shoulder) and Christian Watson (ankle). The Lions are coming off their bye. Every player on the roster practiced, including safety Brian Branch, who is set to return from last year’s torn Achilles. Limited participation: LG Aaron Banks (knee/toe), DT Anthony Campbell (ankle), CB Brandon Cisse (hip), WR Matthew Golden (shoulder), QB Jordan Love (back), DT Jordon Riley (Achilles), CB Benjamin St-Juste (hamstring), WR Christian Watson (ankle), WR Savion Williams (ankle). Riley has been designated to return from injured reserve and is within his 21-day practice windows. Limited participation: CB Rock Ya-Sin (hamstring). Packers-Lions Wednesday Injury Report: Here’s What Jordan Love Said About Sore Back Skip to main content SI.COM GREEN BAY, Wis. – Jordan Love has taken a beating at times this season. For the first time, it’s shown on the injury report. He said “no” when asked if he was concerned that he will not be in the lineup against Detroit. Coming off a Sunday night game and with a Thursday night game looming against the Panthers, coach Matt LaFleur conducted a “jog-through” practice on Wednesday but will put the team in pads for a “really good” practice on Thursday. That was welcome news for Love. After two games of strong pass protection in wins over Tampa Bay and Chicago, it was another painful week for Love in the win over Dallas. “It’s just dealing with a sore back from the game,” he said. “Just some lingering effects from that. One of those things, we’ll just take it day by day but, obviously, it was nice to have a jog-through day, a little bit more mental day, and just recover.” By the official stats, Love and Cleveland’s Deshaun Watson have absorbed a league-high 45 hits through Week 6. He was hit eight times and sacked on three against the Cowboys. “Obviously, just with the back, I don’t know exactly what play it happened on, when it happened,” Love said. “We talk about all the time: You want to, obviously, limit me taking hits in the pocket. That’s something that we’ve talked about, we harp on, and there’s been some better efforts to do better and protect better. I think guys are responding to that. It’s one of those things, yeah, you want to be able to limit as many hits as I take.” Running back Josh Jacobs, who is returning after six weeks on the exempt list, is not on the injury report. “I’ve been actually practicing with my helmet and shoulder pads, so it’s not like it’s overly different,” Jacobs said. “I don’t know where we’re going to be at this week, or if I’m actually going to play or not. home.blurb: Good news broke on the Lions' injury front on Tuesday when cornerback Rock Ya-Sin made his practice return. Ya-Sin was inactive in the Lions' Week 5 date at the Arizona Cardinals with a hamstring injury . Both Branch and Mays were listed as full participants, while Ya-Sin was tabbed as a limited participant. Here's a look at Detroit's estimated practice report on Wednesday: Limited participation: LG Aaron Banks (knee/toe), DL Anthony Campbell (ankle), CB Brandon Cisse (shoulder/neck), WR Matthew Golden (shoulder), QB Jordan Love (back), DL Jordon Riley (Achilles), CB Benjamin St-Juste (hamstring), WR Christian Watson (ankle), WR Savion Williams (ankle) Despite a winning record, the Lions currently sit in last place in the NFC North standings . The NFC North is one of just two NFL divisions where every team has a winning record , joining the AFC North in that distinction. That adds to the magnitude of this week's home date against the Packers. Safety Brian Branch and center Cade Mays are both making their returns this week against the Packers . Neither were listed on the Lions' initial injury report. Lions head coach Dan Campbell said in his Wednesday radio appearance that Mays would start at center against Green Bay . picks.blurb: NFL Week 7 picks and predictions, straight-up and ATS: Chiefs upend Seahawks, Raiders scare Rams Skip to main content NFL NFL Standings NFL Free Agency NFL News by Team More NFL News Our NFL Sites MLB Standings MLB Trades and Transactions MLB Free Agency Baseball Insiders MLB News by Team More MLB News Our MLB Sites Draft Tracker NBA Free Agency NBA Standings NBA News by Team More NBA News Our NBA Sites Anaheim Ducks Boston Bruins Buffalo Sabres Calgary Flames Carolina Hurricanes Chicago Blackhawks Colorado Avalanche Columbus Blue Jackets Detroit Red Wings Edmonton Oilers Florida Panthers Los Angeles Kings Minnesota Wild Montreal Canadiens Nashville Predators New Jersey Devils New York Islanders New York Rangers Ottawa Senators Philadelphia Flyers Pittsburgh Penguins San Jose Sharks Seattle Kraken St. Louis Blues Tampa Bay Lightning Toronto Maple Leafs Vancouver Canucks Vegas Golden Knights Washington Capitals Winnipeg Jets COLLEGE College Football Men's College Basketball Women's College Basketball Men's College Baseball ABOUT Contact Meet the Editorial Team Our Entertainment Sites The Kansas City Chiefs have been as reliable as possible, the Seattle Seahawks and Los Angeles Rams have not, the Las Vegas Raiders seem like they just won't go away, and it's safe to say the regular season has gotten off to a wild and weird start as we head into NFL Week 7 . Our picks and predictions each week have been indicative of that. Sorry I didn't have the Arizona Cardinals beating the Rams outright or the Tennessee Titans getting their first win of the season. We persevere and keep going with the picks. It's going to be a fun Week 7 in the league, as the NFL has big-time matchups like Cowboys-Eagles (less exciting than it once was), Chiefs-Seahawks, Rams-Raiders, Packers-Lions and even Patriots-Bears on Thursday night. That's enough to set the stage alone, so let's get right into our NFL Week 7 picks with predictions straight-up and against the spread for every game this week. NFL Week 7 predictions: Picks straight-up and ATS for every game Las Vegas Raiders quarterback Kirk Cousins | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect NFL Week 7 Matchup Straight-Up Pick Patriots vs. Bears (TNF) Steelers vs. Saints (Paris) Buccaneers vs. Panthers Panthers -3.5 49ers vs. Falcons Bengals vs. Ravens Giants vs. Texans Dolphins vs. Jets Browns vs. Titans Colts vs. Vikings Broncos vs. Cardinals Cardinals +4.5 Rams vs. Raiders Packers vs. Lions Chiefs vs. Seahawks Cowboys vs. Eagles 2026 NFL Picks Straight-Up Record: 58-35 (Last week 7-7) | ATS Record: 43-48-2 (Last week 6-8) Note: All lines are courtesy of FanDuel Sportsbook. Game odds refresh periodically and are subject to change. If you or someone you know has a gambling problem and wants help, call 1-800-GAMBLER. Toughest NFL Week 7 prediction to make Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Kansas City Chiefs (+2.5) vs. Seattle Seahawks Kansas City Chiefs (+2.5) vs. Seattle Seahawks Frankly, there were a lot of tough predictions to make, but taking the Chiefs to go on the road to Seattle and hand the Seahawks another loss outright feels like the one I struggled with the most. With all due respect to the 12th Man and the impact that could have on this game, there's a lot to be worried about when it comes to the Seahawks right now. Sam Darnold and this offense are in dire straits, particularly with their inability to effectively run the ball, which then puts it all on the shoulders of a quarterback who, outside of the playoffs last year, has been exceptionally turnover-prone. That then, in turn, puts way too much pressure on this defense. Then there's the Chiefs, a team that has a defense under Steve Spagnuolo that feels tailor-made to be able to put Darnold into turnover-prone positions in this game. Now, to be sure, the Kansas City passing offense hasn't been operating on all cylinders, so I do wonder what Mike Macdonald will have in store to try and bottle up Kenneth Walker III. At the end of the day, though, there's simply more I trust with the Chiefs right now than with Seahawks, so even on the road, give me KC. Easiest NFL Week 7 pick on the board New York Jets quarterback Geno Smith | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Miami Dolphins vs. New York Jets (-4.5) Miami Dolphins vs. New York Jets (-4.5) Don't mistake this for having any type of unwavering faith in the New York Jets. It's wavering quite a bit. At the same time, maybe the thing that I'm most confident in right now is the fact that the Miami Dolphins are the worst team in the NFL. Yes, they might win a game randomly at some point this season, but I have a hard time believing that win comes on the road and that it comes against a team that is at least as healthy as the Jets are right now in this moment. The Dolphins don't have anyone that can cover Garrett Wilson or even Omar Cooper Jr. in the passing game, which should give Geno Smith some consistent options in the pass game, while Braelon Allen and the offensive line are getting the run game clicking. The defense is fine overall, but the pass rush against a team that's not without De'Von Achane leads me to believe that Malik Willis is going to have a tough time on Sunday. This feels almost too simple, but I can't pass it up. The pick that probably has you scratching your head Arizona Cardinals quarterback Jacoby Brissett | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Denver Broncos vs. Arizona Cardinals (+4.5) Denver Broncos vs. Arizona Cardinals (+4.5) I know, I know, I know. My Bo Nix slander has gone entirely too far. I can hear you complaining about it now, and it's a fair point, because even after beating the Rams, I'm under no guise that the Cardinals are a high-quality football team. At the same time, though, Nix is playing like the worst quarterback in the NFL right now. Even as someone low on Nix, I didn't expect this type of dramatic dropoff with no real signs of things getting any better. The Cardinals defense is certainly a generous unit, but I don't know if Sean Payton or Nix himself have enough faith in the quarterback right now to fully take advantage of that. Moreover, the defense has, on the whole, been lesser than a year ago and has been quite banged up. While the ceiling of the Cardinals is low, I don't think that Jacoby Brissett is going to make the same back-breaking mistakes we saw Sam Darnold make on Thursday Night Football last week. This feels like a game that could end up being similarly weird to Arizona's win over the Rams this past week, and I'm not only taking the Cards against the spread in this matchup, but give me them to pull off the upset fully while playing at home. away.headline: Rams' rampant injuries are not a free meal ticket for the Raiders in Week 7
away.blurb: All-world defensive end Myles Garrett has been on the shelf for weeks and will not return to face Las Vegas in Week 7. But that is just the tip of the iceberg for the surprisingly 2-4 Rams. They'll also be without Davante Adams, Kobie Turner, Poona Ford, and potentially Trent McDuffie and Nate Landman. Landman is the Rams' starting WILL linebacker, and he makes a lot of good plays against the run and in space. It remains to be seen if he or McDuffie will play, but them starting the week as a DNP is not necessarily a good sign, and they could be playing at less than 100% if they do suit up. Raiders should remember Patriots beatdown and not count out injured foes Remember how confident fans were going into Week 5's game against the New England Patriots because they were down their top four cornerbacks and several other key players were limited or non-participants during the week? Rhamondre Stevenson, Christian Barmore, Christian Elliss, etc. If the Las Vegas Raiders want to right the ship in Week 7 and put an end to their three-game skid, it starts with addressing their own issues. Self-scouting is so important in the NFL. But the Los Angeles Rams are also coming into town this Sunday, and they are never an easy group to topple. Led by Sean McVay, one of the most brilliant minds in the sport, and with a star-studded roster that is apprepo for the city that they call home, the Rams pose significant challenges for a young Raiders team and coaching staff. As luck would have it for Las Vegas, though, LA is majorly banged up. They're not just dealing with depth injuries, either; several of their game-changers and biggest contributors will be on the sideline when the two teams take the field at Allegiant Stadium. That may sound like a free meal ticket and a huge advantage for the Silver and Black, and it is, in some ways. But the Raiders just learned in Week 5 that facing a short-staffed roster does not automatically lead to a win. In fact, it was a big, embarrassing lesson that they can't forget and surely haven't still less than two weeks removed from it. Key Rams injuries have piled up recently, and this week is the worst yet Adams went down with a ruptured hamstring in last week's loss to the Arizona Cardinals, and both Turner and Ford got hurt as well. Los Angeles isn't particularly deep at wide receiver, so it'll basically be Puka Nacua and some players that the Raiders wouldn't otherwise circle on the scouting report. Given Las Vegas' issues on the interior offensive line in recent weeks, the Rams not having Turner is massive. He's been a dual-threat this year, stopping the run and getting after the quarterback, so with Turner not playing, the Silver and Black have a lot less to worry about. This becomes especially true when one factors in the absence of Ford, who is a big nose tackle capable of plugging several holes by himself. Ford doesn't play many pass-rush snaps, but he is adequate in that realm as well. No Ford and no Turner is a godsend fo

away.headline: This hypothetical trade would solve Rams' 2026 kicking problems
away.blurb: ESPN's Bill Barnwell proposed that the Rams trade for Indianapolis Colts kicker Spencer Shrader in a move that would immediately solve their biggest special teams issue. In his trade deadline pitches, Barnwell wrote that Los Angeles would acquire Shrader from the Colts for a 2027 fifth-round pick. Playing his home games in a dome obviously helps, but Shrader is one of the league’s most accurate kickers, and he won’t be an unrestricted free agent until 2028. He is a useful player for the Colts, but he’s also not an essential piece for a team that’s rebuilding. The Rams are already on their third kicker of the season. They cut Harrison Mevis , who went 5-of-9 on field goals (55.6%) with a long of 48. Blake Grupe, who made his only attempt, is on injured reserve after just one game. L.A. then signed veteran Brandon McManus as a stopgap despite some bad misses a year ago. Shrader, 27, has made 36 of 37 career field goals and 35 of 36 extra points, including 6-for-6 on field goals from 50-plus yards this season. He leads the NFL in 2026 with 18 of 18 made field goals. He's also gone 12 of 13 on extra points. Kicker trades are rare, and the price is usually low. There have been just seven trades involving a kicker since 2020, and the most recent was Washington acquiring Cade York from Cleveland in August 2024 for a conditional seventh-round pick. Every deal on the list was built around a seventh-rounder, so Barnwell’s proposed fifth-round pick for Shrader would be well above that going rate. But to solve a big problem for a contending team, it might be worth it for Los Angeles. We may earn a commission when you buy through links on this page. away.headline: Rams QB Matthew Stafford Sends Blunt Message to Fantasy Football Players
away.blurb: “Everybody sees these and they’re on their fantasy team or whatever, and they’re like, ‘I gotta trade a guy in and out now.’ And we’re like, ‘That guy’s worked his [expletive] off for eight months to get this opportunity and it’s unfortunate he doesn’t get to do what he loves to do,’” Stafford said. Stafford said sitting out eats at Adams. “I know how hard he works to be out there for us, and when he’s not able to do that it tears him up,” he added. On the injury report, All-Pro cornerback Trent McDuffie didn’t practice Oct. 21 after a groin issue kept him out against Arizona. Fantasy managers see a roster problem when a player goes down, but Matthew Stafford sees a teammate robbed of the work he put in. The Los Angeles Rams quarterback addressed his team’s injury list on Oct. 21. Head coach Sean McVay expects wide receiver Davante Adams to sit six to 10 weeks with an injured hamstring. Stafford, the reigning NFL MVP, said fan reactions miss the real loss. Los Angeles fell to 2-4 with an 18-16 loss to the Arizona Cardinals on Oct. 18, its second straight defeat. Defensive lineman Poona Ford ruptured his triceps in that game and is done for the year. Fellow lineman Kobie Turner, who strained his groin, went to injured reserve. McVay said Oct. 19 that linebacker Nate Landman is going through the concussion protocol. Edge rusher Myles Garrett and tight end Terrance Ferguson are still on IR. In his 18th NFL season, Stafford has 11 touchdown passes and six interceptions. He sees this slide as a leadership test. “That’s when my role becomes even more important as a leader, as somebody that can try and help steady the ship for us,” he said. The Rams visit the Las Vegas Raiders on Oct. 25, then face the Los Angeles Chargers, Washington Commanders , and Cardinals before their bye.

away.headline: Rams-Raiders injury report: Trent McDuffie, Nate Landman miss practice
away.source: USA TODAY Touchdown Wire on MSN
away.blurb: On Wednesday, Trent McDuffie and Nate Landman both missed practice. Landman is in the concussion protocol, while McDuffie is still recovering from a groin injury that caused him to sit out Week 6 against the Cardinals. Defensive tackle Tonka Hemingway was the only non-participant for the Raiders. Five other players were limited, including Brock Bowers and Kolton Miller. After dropping their last two games, the Los Angeles Rams are back to work in advance of their Week 7 matchup with the Las Vegas Raiders . The injury bug bit the Rams hard on Sunday, as Davante Adams, Kobie Turner, Poona Ford and Blake Grupe were all lost to IR, so Los Angeles will be shorthanded against Vegas this week. They won't make any excuses, though. Sean McVay said the Rams are monitoring McDuffie's progress to see if he'll be ready to go against the Raiders. home.headline: Rams' rampant injuries are not a free meal ticket for the Raiders in Week 7
home.blurb: All-world defensive end Myles Garrett has been on the shelf for weeks and will not return to face Las Vegas in Week 7. But that is just the tip of the iceberg for the surprisingly 2-4 Rams. They'll also be without Davante Adams, Kobie Turner, Poona Ford, and potentially Trent McDuffie and Nate Landman. Landman is the Rams' starting WILL linebacker, and he makes a lot of good plays against the run and in space. It remains to be seen if he or McDuffie will play, but them starting the week as a DNP is not necessarily a good sign, and they could be playing at less than 100% if they do suit up. Raiders should remember Patriots beatdown and not count out injured foes Remember how confident fans were going into Week 5's game against the New England Patriots because they were down their top four cornerbacks and several other key players were limited or non-participants during the week? Rhamondre Stevenson, Christian Barmore, Christian Elliss, etc. If the Las Vegas Raiders want to right the ship in Week 7 and put an end to their three-game skid, it starts with addressing their own issues. Self-scouting is so important in the NFL. But the Los Angeles Rams are also coming into town this Sunday, and they are never an easy group to topple. Led by Sean McVay, one of the most brilliant minds in the sport, and with a star-studded roster that is apprepo for the city that they call home, the Rams pose significant challenges for a young Raiders team and coaching staff. As luck would have it for Las Vegas, though, LA is majorly banged up. They're not just dealing with depth injuries, either; several of their game-changers and biggest contributors will be on the sideline when the two teams take the field at Allegiant Stadium. That may sound like a free meal ticket and a huge advantage for the Silver and Black, and it is, in some ways. But the Raiders just learned in Week 5 that facing a short-staffed roster does not automatically lead to a win. In fact, it was a big, embarrassing lesson that they can't forget and surely haven't still less than two weeks removed from it. Key Rams injuries have piled up recently, and this week is the worst yet Adams went down with a ruptured hamstring in last week's loss to the Arizona Cardinals, and both Turner and Ford got hurt as well. Los Angeles isn't particularly deep at wide receiver, so it'll basically be Puka Nacua and some players that the Raiders wouldn't otherwise circle on the scouting report. Given Las Vegas' issues on the interior offensive line in recent weeks, the Rams not having Turner is massive. He's been a dual-threat this year, stopping the run and getting after the quarterback, so with Turner not playing, the Silver and Black have a lot less to worry about. This becomes especially true when one factors in the absence of Ford, who is a big nose tackle capable of plugging several holes by himself. The Las Vegas Raiders received encouraging news regarding Ashton Jeanty's health as the team prepares for Sunday's matchup against the Buffalo Bills. After spending much of the season dealing with foot and ankle injuries, the second-year running back appears to be making significant progress. Speaking with reporters at his locker Thursday, Jeanty said he was feeling great and that this was the best he had felt all season, according to ESPN reporter Ryan McFadden. "He's playing," Kubiak said when asked about potentially sitting Jeanty. Kubiak also noted that Jeanty was making progress in his recovery, raising the possibility that he could take on a larger workload during practice. Jeanty's comments Thursday offered further encouragement, suggesting that the running back is beginning to feel more comfortable after battling injuries throughout the season. The former Boise State standout first suffered an ankle injury during training camp in August. While he recovered in time for the regular season, the issue has continued to linger, making it difficult for him to play at full strength. Jeanty appeared to aggravate the ankle during Las Vegas' Week 4 loss to the Kansas City Chiefs before dealing with an additional foot issue ahead of last Sunday's matchup against the New England Patriots.

home.headline: Bills' Sam Franklin Jr. Suspended by NFL for Spitting at Raiders, Joins CJGJ in Missing Week 8
home.blurb: Buffalo Bills defensive back Sam Franklin Jr. landed in some hot water for an incident during the team's Week 6 win over the Las Vegas Raiders. The NFL announced that Franklin has been suspended for one game for "an act of unsportsmanlike conduct" after he was seen spitting at an opponent in the fourth quarter of Sunday's game. The Bills are on a bye this week, so Franklin will miss their Week 8 matchup against the Baltimore Ravens. According to ESPN's Adam Schefter , Franklin "is denying the allegation and will appeal." Franklin joined the Bills' practice squad prior to the 2025 season and quickly earned a spot on the main roster. He appeared in all 17 games last season, mostly on special teams. He was voted a team captain this season. While Franklin is denying the allegation, it seems like the Bills had a hard time keeping their mouths shut during Sunday's contest. Veteran safety C.J. Gardner-Johnson also received a one-game suspension after cameras caught him spitting toward Raiders tight end Brock Bowers and center Tyler Linderbaum. "C.J. knows that it's hard enough to win in this league with 48 guys, much less 47. He knows that that can't happen. It's inexcusable. That's not the standard that we're going to have and play with," Bills head coach Joe Brady told reporters on Monday. "He's addressed it. It's been addressed. The league came down with the suspension. … We want to toe the line with everything we do but we can't cross the line." Gardner-Johnson addressed the incident with his teammates and coaches after the game, and he posted an apology for his actions on social media. "My passion and competitive nature have always been a huge part of who I am, but I also understand that there is a line that should never be crossed," he wrote. "The gesture I made toward my opponent was inappropriate, unnecessary, and not a reflection of the respect I have for him or this game." The Bills will try to focus on avoiding any further incidents during their bye week before returning to action on Nov. 1 against the Ravens.

Mike Kadlick Week 7 Upset Pick Miami Dolphins (+190) vs. New York Jets It’s time for the Dolphins to notch their first win of the Jeff Hafley era. While Miami currently owns the NFL’s worst offense and a bottom-10 defense, they’re coming off a bye week and are playing a Jets team that has lost four of its last five games. Though they’ve played competitively for the most part, New York has still yet to find an identity under coach Aaron Glenn and could be ripe for the taking after losing to the Patriots in Foxborough in Week 6. I think Miami finds their way to victory on Sunday at MetLife. Iain MacMillan Week 7 Upset Pick Tampa Bay Buccaneers (+140) vs. Carolina Panthers It's time to sell high on this Panthers team. Their offense has been phenomenal to start the year, but I have plenty of questions surrounding the ability of some of the defenses they've had to face. Once they started facing top-10 defenses, I wouldn't be surprised to see them significantly regress. It could start this weekend when they take on a Tampa Bay defense that's fourth in opponent EPA per play and eighth in opponent success rate. I'm going to get in on the Bucs early this week and hope that Baker Mayfield ends up returning to action. If he starts on Sunday, we'll likely get some nice closing line value on the Buccaneers. Peter Dewey Week 7 Upset Pick Kansas City Chiefs (+124) vs. Seattle Seahawks This may be the biggest test for Patrick Mahomes and the Chiefs so far this season, as Seattle has the No. 1 defense in yards per play allowed and the No. 2 defense in EPA/Play. Yet, I’m taking Kansas City to win outright on the road and improve to 6-0. The Chiefs have found a new dynamic with Kenneth Walker III and this running game, and I expect the reigning Super Bowl MVP to have a major workload against his former team. Mahomes is a shocking 10-1-1 against the spread and 9-3 straight up as a road underdog in his career, and he’s by far the better quarterback in this game. Sam Darnold has doomed Seattle at times this season, throwing seven picks in four games since returning from a glute injury. The Seahawks offense has been extremely reliant on Jaxon Smith-Njigba, and it ranks 25th in the league in EPA/Play and 20th in success rate. picks.blurb: The dynamic running back broke free of his platoon in Washington state after being deemed expendable despite the Seahawks' $700 million in contract extensions to keep its core intact. That made him the balm in a terribly burned Kansas City Chiefs backfield, where he's put up an Offensive Player of the Year pace across the team's 5-0 start. Now he faces his former team in his former home in primetime. That game has us torn in Week 7. It's not the only one. Welcome back to For The Win's straight-up, moneyline NFL picks column. I ended 2023 as Pickwatch’s top expert in a field of hundreds. The two seasons that followed? Ehhhhh, we don't like to talk about that. But I'm back and hopeful I'll either be good enough to rejoin the top 25 or, barring that, be so destructively bad you're left with no choice but to fade my picks all the way to prosperity. Joining me for 2026 is a six-person panel ranging from FTW editors (Charles Curtis, Wajih AlBaroudi and Jeff Smith) to betting analysts (Prince Grimes) to NFL writers (Robert Zeglinski and Andrew Joseph). Here are our Week 7 picks. Patriots at Bears Steelers at Saints Bengals at Ravens Browns at Titans Colts at Vikings Dolphins at Jets Giants at Texans 49ers at Falcons Bucs at Panthers Broncos at Cardinals Packers at Lions Rams at Raiders Chiefs at Seahawks Cowboys at Eagles Season to date: Since our editing software occasionally struggles to make these picks super clear, here they are in an easier to read (but impossible to cut and paste) .jpg you can click to expand: Let's break out three games to talk about. Survivor pick of the week: New York Jets (-4.5) over the Miami Dolphins Cool, I've murdered you once again. While I appreciate some Indianapolis Colts schadenfreude, I'm truly not enjoying this year's survivor slate. Ah well, time to back another flawed team with a quarterback working through yet another redemption arc. The Dolphins are coming off a bye and scored 24 points their last time out, but that was also the only week this season in which they've topped 13. New York's defense is competent. The Jets offense just got a boost with Omar Cooper Jr. returning to the lineup. Geno Smith faces the league's second-worst passing defense. If he can't thrive here, it's time to fade back into "high value backup" status. Last week : 1-0 Season to date : 3-3 Hardest favorite to back: Baltimore Ravens (-1.5) over the Cincinnati Bengals Oh, friends, do I ever hate this pick. We're writing this on Wednesday and don't know what Lamar Jackson has planned for the week. If he's playing? I'm in. If not? This flips to Joe Shiesty and company. But, for now, let's assume we get an 80 percent Jackson behind center. Why I like this pick : The AFC North isn't defined by logic and answers only to the gods of chaos and violence. Baltimore has fielded the slightly better defense, and an emerging Ja'Kobi Lane brings an important fallback option. The Ravens find an extra gear against Cincinnati, beating the Bengals five of their last six tries and scoring at least 24 points in each of those wins. Why I don't like this pick : Even if Jackson plays, he'll have to face a revitalized and suddenly viable Bengals pass rush that has a strategy beyond "throw Trey Hendrickson at them, hope it works." The Bengals have the manpower to blitz effectively and the defensive backs to stand up in single coverage. Baltimore's top-heavy receiving corps will be put to the test, and it may take a Lane or a Devontez Walker to lift this team up in a high-scoring affair. Those Ravens wins came under Jim Harbaugh. Jesse Minter might be able to take up his mantle, but those are big shoes to fill seven weeks into his rookie season. Even worse, Cincinnati is coming off a bye. Season to date : 5-1 Upset pick of the week: Kansas City Chiefs (+2.5) over the Seattle Seahawks Kenneth Walker III's respectful revenge game! The reigning Super Bowl MVP has been masterful at unclogging a previously stagnant Chiefs offense. Now he faces a defense he knows well. Will he leave Lumen Field with yet another win? The Chiefs are rolling right now. The Seahawks are not. The Super Bowl mainstay has rebounded from its uncharacteristic 2025 falloff by letting Walker cook. Kansas City has a top 10 passing offense in terms of expected points added (EPA) but is No. 1 by a wide margin when it comes to the run game . The Seahawks' run defense ranks third, which means this game is probably gonna be a pleasant reminder why we love this dumb sport so much. But Kansas City can counter with Patrick Mahomes. The Seahawks have Sam Darnold, who appears adrift without former coordinator Klint Kubiak, now head coach of the Las Vegas Raiders . Darnold's -0.050 EPA per dropback ranks 28th in the league. He's struggled to connect with anyone not named Jaxon Smith-Njigba and the Chiefs have fielded a top four passing offense this season. The Seahawks are at home and facing a breaking point when it comes to the NFC West race. Dropping under .500 could give the San Francisco 49ers a four-game lead in the division, and while there are still 10 games to be played for both teams, that's a deep hole to dig out of. Seattle's fans understand that, and they're going to be LOUD as evening descends on the Emerald City. The Chiefs have gotten better returns than expected from their receivers, but asking Xavier Worthy and Jalen Royals to shine against the Seattle secondary is a monumental ask. Even in a 3-3 start the Seahawks defense ranks second only to the Minnesota Vikings in overall efficiency through six weeks. Heading into Week 7 against the Seattle Seahawks , the Chiefs are 5-0. What's so impressive about this record is that they've done this despite some significant injury issues on the offensive side of the ball. Rashee Rice is banged up and has missed time, Tyquan Thornton is done for the year, and Josh Simmons has yet to play this year. Unfortunately, Simmons' injury isn't getting any better. According to ESPN's Nate Taylor , the Chiefs' head trainer revealed Simmons has "plateaued" in his rehab process, and the first-round offensive tackle will be hitting injured reserve this season. Chiefs to place Josh Simmons on IR as injury recovery has 'plateaued' "Chiefs head trainer Rick Burkholder said Josh Simmons (bulging disc in lower back) is going to be placed on IR," Taylor reports. This is a brutal blow for the Chiefs, as Simmons was supposed to be the team's starting left tackle, but he's yet to play a single game this season due to injury. Burkholder revealed why Simmons isn't coming back, beyond simply the bulging disc in his back causing an issue. "Josh worked his tail off & diligent every day," Burkholder said per Taylor. "However, we feel he's plateaued in the rehab process. He's just not there yet." While the placement of Simmons on IR is a tough blow, the reasoning for it makes the decision hurt that much more. So, with the Chiefs' OT not getting any better, they've decided to place him on IR. This means that Khalil Benson will remain the team's starting left tackle while Simmons recovers from this back injury. While this isn't an issue that'll require surgery, it's still a huge piece of news for the Chiefs and their offense, as their first-round offensive tackle meant to anchor this line, and has impressed when he's been on the field, is now going to miss at least four more games.
