Seattle's ground game has struggled without Charbonnet and first-round pick Jadarian Price (chest/shoulder), who has been on injured reserve since Week 2. Seahawks starting weakside linebacker Drake Thomas (ankle), who sat out last Thursday, missed practice on Wednesday. Fellow linebacker Tyrice Knight (oblique) and wide receiver Rashid Shaheed (hip) were among the players who were limited. Chiefs right tackle Jaylon Moore (concussion) and wide receiver Rashee Rice (hamstring/knee) also missed practice. It remains unclear when left tackle Josh Simmons (back), who sat out Wednesday, will make his season debut. The NFL's top rusher will lead his new team, the Kansas City Chiefs (5-0), into a primetime matchup Sunday against the defending NFL champion Seahawks (3-3), for whom he won the Super Bowl MVP award last season. "I'm just focused on critiquing the mistakes we made," said Walker, referring to last weekend's sluggish 22-6 victory against the winless Los Angeles Chargers. "Once we get to that point (Seattle), we'll see." For the soft-spoken Walker, that wasn't surprising. But others, on both teams, had plenty to say. "I know it's going to be a special moment for him to get back to the place where you kind of built your career and won a Super Bowl," Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes said. " ... But at the end of the day, we have to win a football game." Seahawks safety Julian Love said it's been "weird for sure" watching film of Walker break off long runs for the Chiefs. "He's doing what he did for us last season, the past bunch of seasons for the Seahawks. And he's picked up where he left off from last season," Love said. "His tape looks incredible. And so it's all hands on deck to try to contain and try to stop him." Walker, who signed a three-year, $43.05 million deal with the Chiefs in the offseason as a free agent, leads all NFL running backs with 665 yards rushing and 6.3 yards per attempt. His six rushing touchdowns are two behind Buffalo quarterback Josh Allen, though he's played in one fewer game because of Kansas City's early bye week. Walker rushed for 135 yards on 27 carries in the Seahawks' 29-13 victory against New England in the Super Bowl. home.blurb: The Kansas City Chiefs have released their first injury report ahead of Week 7 against the Seattle Seahawks. After being a limited participant in practice all of last week with a back injury, Chiefs starting LT Josh Simmons is back to being a non-participant. The difference this time? Simmons is now being listed with both the back injury and a “personal” designation. You might recall the 2025 NFL season, when Simmons missed four weeks due to a personal family matter. When he returned, Simmons broke his wrist and ultimately played in just eight total games that year. It's unclear what the “personal” designation refers to, but The Athletic's Jesse Newell said Simmons was in the locker room ahead of practice . Here’s a quick breakdown of each team's Week 7 injury report. Keep in mind that clubs can add to the injury report through kickoff on Sunday. They will release game status designations on Friday, Oct. 23. KEY: DNP = Did not participate | LP = Limited participation | FP = Full participation | NIR = Not injury related Cooper McDonald was limited in his first practice back since returning from injured reserve . This is part of the normal ramp-up process. Travis Kelce is listed as limited after “tweaking” his ankle in Week 6's game against the Chargers. I expected this for the veteran , but I don't anticipate him being at risk of missing Sunday's game. home.blurb: Leading into Week 6, the Chiefs had starting left tackle Josh Simmons back at practice in a limited capacity for all three sessions . Before last week, Simmons hadn't practiced since Aug. 16. Asked about his potential status for Sunday's game against the Seahawks, Reid was hesitant to overpromise. The team will continue to ramp up Simmons' workload and see how he responds as he returns from injury. The Chiefs could realistically be without two of their most experienced offensive tackles, Moore and Simmons. That would leave Kahlil Benson as the starting left tackle and Joshua Ezeudu as the starting right tackle. Diego Pounds would also be active for the first time since Kansas City acquired him in a trade , should Moore be out with his concussion. Reid discussed Ezeudu's Week 6 performance on Monday. The trade acquisition filled in for Moore after the concussion just before halftime against the Chargers. “I appreciated the guys and how they played yesterday,” Reid said “Josh (Ezeudu) jumped in and played at the right tackle spot. I thought he did a nice job there. So, and he's got experience. I'm not real worried about all that.” In 17 pass-blocking snaps on Sunday , Ezeudu allowed just one hurry per Pro Football Focus. The Chiefs put him in a good spot to be successful in that game. With a full week of practice and preparation as a potential starter, Ezeudu could deliver an even better performance against Seattle. Moore could realistically practice and play this week. It's not out of the question. It's happened before. However, concussions typically mean that you're slated to miss at least one week of the season. An independent neurologist must clear him before he can return to play. home.headline: Kansas City Chiefs trade acquisition in line for his first start as offensive line injuries linger into first practice for Week 7 vs. Seahawks
home.blurb: The Kansas City Chiefs could trot out a third starting offensive line combination of the 2026 NFL season in Seattle. Wednesday's practice offered few encouraging signs for a pair of injured tackles. Chiefs head coach Andy Reid confirmed Wednesday that starting right tackle Jaylon Moore remains in the NFL's concussion protocol . Moore must clear the league's return-to-play protocols to suit up against the Seahawks. According to Reid, he would not participate in Wednesday's practice. What Are the NFL's Return-to-Play Protocols for Concussions? Players placed in the NFL concussion protocol must complete five phases without symptoms before they can be cleared to return to play. Symptom-limited activity: Light stretching and stationary bike riding. It remains to be seen whether Moore can clear those protocols ahead of the Week 7 matchup. However, sitting out of practice entirely on Wednesday isn't a good start. So who is in line to start at right tackle? Fans would hope starting left tackle Josh Simmons could return to the lineup after he practiced in a limited capacity ahead of Week 6's game against the Los Angeles Chargers. That didn't look promising on Wednesday. Reporters didn't spot Simmons on the field during their brief look at team stretch and warm-ups. Reid also didn't mention Simmons' status when he addressed injured players. He spoke only about Moore and wide receiver Rashee Rice, who also did not practice. Simmons did return to practice in a limited capacity last week. Still, clips captured during the brief window the team gives media members ahead of practice made it clear Simmons wasn't 100%. He was seen grimacing while stretching , and he simply didn't look right while jogging on the field. It very much looks like the back injury will keep him out longer. Reid's comments on Monday suggested the Chiefs are continuing to work through his back issue while ramping up his workload. Again, missing practice Wednesday doesn't set him up for a likely Week 7 return. The Houston Texans are officially back, as is Caleb Williams with the Chicago Bears , and we have some serious questions about the Los Angeles Rams , who were upset by the Arizona Cardinals at home last Sunday. The Cardinals now have more wins at SoFi Stadium this year than the Rams and Los Angeles Chargers combined. This week, the Pittsburgh Steelers and New Orleans Saints will play the first-ever NFL game in Paris, the San Francisco 49ers look to remain perfect against the Atlanta Falcons , and Kenneth Walker III aims to lead the Kansas City Chiefs to victory over his former team, the Seattle Seahawks . This could be a revenge game for the ages. Which teams should you pick in Week 7, and which should you fade? CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin are here to break down the biggest games of the weekend. For clarity, lines for these selections were taken on Oct. 21 over at DraftKings Sportsbook. New England Patriots at Chicago Bears (-3) (TNF) Dajani (Bears -3): I can't remember the last time I've been this excited for a Thursday night game. Caleb Williams will suit up for the first time at home since his hamstring injury, and this is the first Bears home game since the passing of Mike Ditka. I have concerns about this Bears pass defense and how it will fare against a red-hot Drake Maye , but the fact is that Chicago has allowed 9.3 points per game at home this season. The Bears' offense has also averaged 35 points per game in their four wins, and I think Williams is out to make a statement. This will be a high-flying affair that comes down to the very end, and a push is very much in play. But give me Chicago at home, with the backing of an emotionally charged atmosphere. Remember, the Bears' lone Super Bowl win came against the New England Patriots under Ditka. … Prediction: Bears 28, Patriots 24 Dubin (Bears -3): I also see this being a high-scoring game, with two offenses that can pile up points quickly. Chicago's offense in two non-rain/non-Brian Flores games with Caleb Williams under center has been electric, particularly on the ground, and Caleb Williams opens things up for the passing game. New England is struggling to run the ball, but Drake Maye has been on fire as of late. I'll lean toward the Bears here because of the Patriots' injury issues along the offensive line, which could hold the run game back further and put even more on Maye's shoulders. … Prediction: Bears 31, Patriots 27 Pittsburgh Steelers (-3.5) vs. New Orleans Saints (Paris) Dajani (Saints +3.5): The Steelers are impossible to figure out. From week-to-week — or even half-to-half, as evidenced by last week's overtime victory against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers . If you're going to give me the hook at +3.5 in an international game, I'm probably going to take it. The Saints are a perfect 8-0 ATS in their last eight games away from home, and are 3-0 ATS all-time in international games. I think Gayle Benson's recent comments stirred up the locker room, and the Saints responded with a win in which they dropped 34 points — even if it came against the New York Giants . … Prediction: Steelers 23, Saints 20 Dubin (Steelers -3.5): The Saints finally played a game from ahead last week against the Giants, and they didn't necessarily look comfortable doing it. They have mostly been a second-half offensive team throughout this season, struggling early on before piling up yards and points in comeback mode. I don't trust this offense enough to build a lead against Pittsburgh's defense (ninth in yards, 12th in points, fifth in EPA per play) right now, so I'll lean toward this game playing out in a similar fashion to New Orleans' early-season contests, with the Steelers taking a lead and the Saints trying to stage a comeback, only to fail this time around. … Prediction: Steelers 21, Saints 17 San Francisco 49ers (-3) at Atlanta Falcons Dajani (Falcons +3): I'm thinking about backing the Falcons in this spot. The 49ers had an emotional victory over the Seahawks in Week 5 and are now on a short week after Monday night's win against the Washington Commanders . It looked like we were in for a blowout after the 49ers went up 23-3, but Washington then outscored San Francisco, 14-0, while outgaining the 49ers 201 yards to 7 yards. That was ... interesting to see. The 49ers have found a way to keep winning games despite all of the injuries. Nick Bosa , Mike Evans , Deebo Samuel , Upton Stout and Mykel Williams were among the players who did not practice on Wednesday. This week, I'm going to take the points with Atlanta. … Prediction: 49ers 22, Falcons 20 Dubin (49ers -3): This line feels several points too low, even with Mike Evans potentially out in addition to all of the other wide receiver issues. So long as the Niners have Kyle Shanahan calling plays and Brock Purdy , Christian McCaffrey and George Kittle involved, I think their offense cooks. And Atlanta can't quite reach the same level offensively — even with Bijan Robinson and Drake London on hand. The Niners have been excellent against the run this year, and if this game winds up being one where Penix has to match Purdy throw for throw, I don't see that going well for Atlanta. … Prediction: 49ers 26, Falcons 16 Cincinnati Bengals at Baltimore Ravens (-3) Dajani ( Bengals +3): The Bengals are fresh off their bye while the Baltimore Ravens are fresh off ... a loss to the Cleveland Browns . It was their 15th loss when leading by at least seven points in the fourth quarter since 2020, which ranks the most in the NFL. Lamar Jackson has a chance to return this week, but I'm curious to see how "spry" he looks. The two-time NFL MVP was playing some fantastic ball before the unfortunate ankle injury, and it's worth mentioning he's 7-2 in his career against Joe Burrow . I was high on the Bengals entering this season, and I'm not ready to move off that take. I think this Baltimore secondary is in for a tough test in stopping Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins . The former averages 120.4 receiving yards per game vs. the Ravens, while the latter caught two touchdowns the last time he faced them. Higgins actually hasn't faced Baltimore since Oct. 6, 2024! It's been a while. Give me the upset here. We aren't 100% sure if Jackson is even returning to the lineup, and he'll have to face one of the best interior pass rushes in the NFL. Dexter Lawrence , Jonathan Allen and Kris Jenkins Jr. are the only defensive tackle trio to record multiple sacks this season. … Prediction: Bengals 29, Ravens 27 Dubin (Ravens -3): I'm assuming that Lamar Jackson is back for this game. If he's not, then you can switch my pick to the Bengals. If Jackson is in alongside Derrick Henry and Zay Flowers , I just don't think this Baltimore offense can be stopped. When those three have shared the field this season, the Ravens are averaging 9.9 yards per play. NINE POINT NINE. Unfortunately, the sample size is only 63 plays due to injuries to Jackson and Flowers at different times. If there is any team that can compete with an explosive offense, it's probably the Bengals, but I don't see them quite keeping up here. … Prediction: Ravens 30, Bengals 26 Green Bay Packers at Detroit Lions (-3) Dajani ( Lions -3): Just take the Over in this matchup. The Lions really burned me coming off the bye last year, losing to J.J. McCarthy , but I'm going to back them in this spot. The concern is, of course, the defense, which ranks dead last in the NFL with 404.4 total yards surrendered per game. HOWEVER, I will mention that Kelvin Sheppard 's unit forced five straight three-and-outs from the Cardinals in that 45-21 win in Week 5. Plus, Brian Branch is set to return to the lineup as well. Give me the Lions at home. … Prediction: Lions 35, Packers 30 Dubin (Lions -3): This one has all the makings of a shootout, with two explosive offenses going back and forth. Jared Goff and Co. are coming off the bye, and they have scored 31 or more points in four of their five games to date — and they scored 26 while piling up 452 yards in the other one. Nobody except maybe Kenneth Walker III is doing it at a higher level than Jahmyr Gibbs right now, either. Meanwhile, Green Bay can throw the ball all over the yard, and everyone throws it on the Lions. Maybe Green Bay can actually run with some efficiency in Josh Jacobs ' potential return, but it's not like he was all that efficient last season, either. I lean toward the Lions because they can beat you both ways. … Prediction: Lions 34, Packers 28 Kansas City Chiefs at Seattle Seahawks (-2.5) (SNF) Dajani (Chiefs +2.5): The Seahawks looked completely disinterested in that Week 6 loss to the Denver Broncos . Dallas is off to a slow start at 2-4, and the defense (31st in EPA/Play) remains one of the worst in the NFL. Dak Prescott and Co. have lost back-to-back primetime games against Tampa Bay (Week 5) and Green Bay (Week 6), looking pretty rough in both appearances. So, can they turn things around on the road against a divisional opponent? The Eagles enter this game on a four-game losing streak, and star quarterback Jalen Hurts is out for the season with blood clots in his lungs. That is a massive blow to the Eagles in the futures market, as they’re now last in the odds to win the NFC East and +15000 to win the Super Bowl. Tanner McKee is set to make another start in Week 7, and this may turn into a lost season for an Eagles team that could decide to trade some veteran pieces to recoup draft capital and lighten the load on the salary cap in years to come. Oddsmakers have set the Cowboys as favorites in this matchup, and a win would put Dallas in a much better position to win the NFC East – which it is still favored to do. away.headline: Remembering the unlikely NFL journey of Cowboys legend Cornell Green
away.blurb: As it turns out, his inexperience with the sport may be what allowed him- and the Cowboys- to tap into his pure athletic ability. But Green turned out to be a very big thing for 13 seasons in Dallas. He made the NFL's All-Rookie team in 1962. The following year, he led the Cowboys in interceptions- a feat he would repeat in 1965, 1966, and 1967. He earned three first-team Al-Pro nods. Went to two Super Bowls, earned one ring. And along the way, he shut down some of the most legendary receivers the game has ever seen. "Cornell Green shut out [the Dolphins' Paul] Warfield," franchise legend Calvin Hill once said, per the team website . "Warfield was like a mega-bomb, and the fact that we were able to prevent him from being who he was – in my mind, the greatest receiver I've ever seen – was remarkable." Green snagged 34 interceptions in his career, in a day when passing was far less popular than it is now. Brandt once theorized that if Green had better hands, he'd have ended his career with three times as many. How could his college's all-time recordholder in rebounding not be better at snatching a football out of the air? Green was once asked. The Cowboys have lost one of their earliest stars, whose improbable path to the NFL-and groundbreaking strides once he arrived- helped pave the way for countless others. Cornell Green, a key member of the Doomsday Defense's first iteration, passed away Wednesday at the age of 86. Green earned five Pro Bowl trips during his career at two different positions- cornerback and safety- and never missed a single game in 13 seasons with the Cowboys, a span which included a streak of 145 consecutive starts over his final 11 years. He played for the first Cowboys squad to go to the Super Bowl, helped the franchise bring home its first Lombardi Trophy, was a Pro Football Hall of Fame nominee for the Senior class of 2026, had his name put forth as a Cowboys Ring of Honor enshrinee as recently as this past spring, and is still- a over a half-century after his retirement- the all-time Cowboys leader in blocked kicks and in the top five in interceptions. Not bad for a kid who never even played college football. Green, born in Oklahoma and raised in northern California, was actually a basketball standout at Utah State and then drafted in 1962 by the NBA's Chicago Zephyrs (who would later become the Washington Bullets and then the Wizards). But it was a time when Cowboys personnel guru Gil Brandt was starting to look to other sports for potential talent to add to the still-fledgling franchise, and he spotted in the 6-foot-4-inch Green a rebounding machine who, as a fifth-round pick, might not make it in the NBA... but could be turned into a football player. Green accepted Brandt's invitation to Cowboys training camp, solely for the $1,000 bonus, fully expecting to get cut in short order and pocket the cash on his way back to Chicago. home.headline: Eagles get good news on Saquon Barkley for Week 7 MNF game vs. Cowboys
home.blurb: According to NFL Network's Mike Garafolo , Barkley is set to return to practice on Thursday, the team's first of the week before they face their NFC East rivals in primetime. Eagles get good news as Saquon Barkley set to return to practice "Eagles RB Saquon Barkley is expected to return to practice today and is in line to play Monday against the Cowboys, sources say," Garafolo reports. He's really only played two full games, as he's missed two games, and was pulled from two others very early due to injuries. This most recent issue, a hamstring, has kept him out of the team's Week 5 and Week 6 matchups. But now, with Garafolo's report before the team's Thursday practice, it seems that Barkley is very close to a return to play on game day, with the expectation that he'll practice, a very good sign he'll be back for the Eagles this week. home.headline: Is Saquon Barkley back from injury vs Cowboys? Latest from Eagles coach
home.blurb: Barkley suffered the injury in the first quarter against the Los Angeles Rams on Oct. 4. He sat out the rest of that game, then the next two games against Jacksonville and Carolina. The Eagles face the Dallas Cowboys on Oct. 26. Eagles coach Nick Sirianni wouldn't say if Barkley will be available against the Cowboys, but he did make it seem like Barkley will participate as the Eagles begin their practice week on Oct. 22. "Saquon's a phenomenal football player, phenomenal leader, captain," Sirianni said. "So anytime you have an opportunity to get someone like him back out on the field, that's huge. We'll see where we are as the week progresses. "Looking forward to seeing him out there [Oct. 22]. "We'll see where we are at the end of it." Sirianni said Barkley's return will boost the Eagles' running game, which ranks 29th in the NFL. The Eagles have especially struggled when quarterbacks Jalen Hurts and Tanner McKee have lined up under center and tried play-action passes. As for other injured players, it's not known yet if edge rushers Jalyx Hunt (knee/ankle), Nolan Smith (concussion) or Jonathan Greenard (ankle) can practice. And left guard Landon Dickerson (knee) is beginning his second week of the 21-day practice window as he works to return from injured reserve. home.headline: Reports: Eagles RB Saquon Barkley to return vs. Cowboys
home.blurb: Oct 22 (Field Level Media) - Philadelphia Eagles running back Saquon Barkley is expected to return to practice Thursday and play against the visiting Dallas Cowboys on Monday night, NFL Network reported. Barkley's return from a hamstring injury sustained early in Week 4 would be a major boost for a team riding a four-game losing streak and reeling from the loss of captain and quarterback Jalen Hurts to a serious blood-clot diagnosis. Philadelphia (2-4) ranks 30th in total offense (255.5 yards per game) and 29th in rushing (82.2) heading into the Week 7 clash with NFC East rival Dallas (2-4). Barkley, 29, was injured in the first quarter of a 24-20 loss to the Los Angeles Rams on Oct. 4. He has rushed 36 times for 182 yards with no touchdowns in four games this season. Named the 2024 NFL Offensive Player of the Year after rushing for 2,005 yards, Barkley has accumulated 11,197 yards and 71 touchdowns from scrimmage in 110 career games (all starts) with the New York Giants (2018-23) and Eagles.

home.headline: NFL will not punish Eagles over handling of Jalen Hurts' blood clots: Report
home.blurb: The Philadelphia Eagles allowed Hurts to play and fly while knowing he had blood clots. The injury has knocked the star quarterback out for the rest of the season.

home.headline: NFL finds Philadelphia Eagles committed no wrongdoing in Jalen Hurts blood clot saga – ‘was handled appropriately’
home.blurb: The quarterback, 28, has been ruled out for the remainder of the season after being diagnosed with deep vein thrombosis and bilateral pulmonary emboli. An Eagles statement previously read, “Out of an abundance of caution, an ultrasound was performed on Saturday following the team’s flight to London and walkthrough. The ultrasound revealed a superficial blood clot. “Our medical staff and doctors in London reviewed the results and concluded that activity and mobility were important and that Jalen could safely play. Doctors recommended a follow-up ultrasound within 72 hours of the game and the return flight to Philadelphia. “On Wednesday night, a follow-up ultrasound revealed movement in the small blood clot. Jalen will be out for Sunday’s game vs. the Panthers as we determine the appropriate course of treatment.
